knowledge_statements.title: Summable-Error Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-summability condition for additive errors in an averaged fixed-point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inexact fixed-point iteration \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k+e^k\) on a Hilbert space, the absolute summable-error regime is the condition \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e^k\rVert<\infty.\] When \(T\) is averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), this condition implies quasi-Fejér stability: the cumulative outward displacement caused by errors is finite. In finite dimensions, the iterates converge to a fixed point of \(T\), and their exact fixed-point residuals satisfy \(\lVert z^k-Tz^k\rVert\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The summable-error regime requires finite total perturbation; for averaged iterations it preserves convergence to a fixed point in finite dimensions.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
\(\sum_k\lVert e^k\rVert<\infty\).
The ambient Hilbert space is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^k\to z^*\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) and \(\lVert z^k-Tz^k\rVert\to0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical summable-error condition for averaged operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition and finite-dimensional convergence consequence are mathematically standard and internally consistent, but the nontrivial averaged-operator convergence claim lacks an authoritative source and locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-relative perturbation condition ensuring sufficient descent of an averaged iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\), and consider \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k+e^k\). A sufficient relative-error regime is \[\lVert e^k\rVert\leq\sigma\lVert z^k-Tz^k\rVert\quad\text{for all }k,\qquad 0\leq\sigma<\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}.\] For every \(z^*\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), this bound leaves a strictly positive net coefficient in the standard averaged-operator descent estimate. Consequently, if the generated sequence is asymptotically regular and every cluster point is fixed, then it converges to a fixed point in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each perturbation is bounded by a fixed fraction of the current fixed-point residual, small enough to retain net descent.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
\(0\leq\sigma<(1-\alpha)/\alpha\).
The iterates are asymptotically regular and all cluster points belong to \(\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative error does not destroy net descent, and \(z^k\) converges to a point in \(\operatorname{Fix}T\) in finite dimensions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound on the additive error does not by itself leave the claimed descent coefficient: expansion of the perturbed squared distance contains a cross term involving the distance to a fixed point, not only the fixed-point residual. Asymptotic regularity and the stated cluster-point condition also do not supply the missing descent or boundedness argument. The threshold and conclusion require an algorithm-specific theorem.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Complexity by Accuracy Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration counts induced by sublinear, linear, and locally superlinear residual rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\geq0\) be the solver's declared residual and \(N(\varepsilon)=\min\{k:r_k\leq\varepsilon\}\). If \(r_k\leq C(k+1)^{-q}\) with \(q>0\), then \[N(\varepsilon)\leq\left\lceil(C/\varepsilon)^{1/q}\right\rceil-1.\] If \(r_k\leq C\rho^k\) with \(0<\rho<1\), then \[N(\varepsilon)\leq\left\lceil\frac{\log(C/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil.\] Hence polynomial residual decay gives polynomial accuracy complexity, whereas linear convergence gives logarithmic accuracy complexity. Any local superlinear tail must be reported separately with its neighborhood and recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual rate of order k to minus q needs polynomially many iterations; geometric decay needs logarithmically many iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<C\).
The residual bounds hold for every iteration counted.
One iteration is the unit of computational work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sublinear decay yields \(N(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-1/q})\), while linear decay yields \(N(\varepsilon)=O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Iteration Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive work model for one operator-splitting iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one solver iteration evaluates \(A\) and \(A^*\) respectively \(n_A\) and \(n_{A^*}\) times, performs \(n_K\) cone projections, and executes \(n_V\) vector operations on vectors of dimension \(d\). If their costs are \(C_A\), \(C_{A^*}\), \(C_K\), and \(O(d)\), respectively, then the per-iteration oracle cost is \[C_{\mathrm{iter}}=n_AC_A+n_{A^*}C_{A^*}+n_KC_K+O(n_Vd).\] Over \(N\) iterations, excluding setup, the total work is \(O(NC_{\mathrm{iter}})\); memory must separately include operator data, cone workspaces, and iteration vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Per-iteration work is the sum of linear-operator, adjoint, cone-projection, and vector-operation costs; total iterative work multiplies this by the iteration count.
assumptions_latex: Oracle counts are uniform over the iterations considered.
Setup and factorization costs are excluded.
Vector operations cost linearly in dimension \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterative work through iteration \(N\) is \(O(NC_{\mathrm{iter}})\).

notation.meaning: Costs of applying the linear operator and its adjoint.
Cost of one complete solver iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Amortization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Average-cost accounting when a fixed affine system is factorized once and reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the affine solve uses a fixed matrix throughout \(N\geq1\) splitting iterations. Let \(F\) be the one-time symbolic and numeric factorization cost, \(S\) the cost of one triangular-solve pair, and \(C\) all remaining per-iteration work. Reusing the factorization gives \[W_N=F+N(S+C),\qquad \frac{W_N}{N}=S+C+\frac{F}{N}.\] Thus the setup contribution per iteration is \(F/N\), and factorization is amortized when \(N\) is large compared with \(F/(S+C)\). Refactorization after data or regularization changes must be charged as an additional setup cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusing one factorization over N iterations reduces its average contribution to the setup cost divided by N.
assumptions_latex: The affine-system matrix is unchanged during the counted iterations.
A stored factorization can be reused for every right-hand side.
\(F,S,C\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The average work per iteration is \(S+C+F/N\), which tends to \(S+C\) as \(N\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Large-Scale Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and storage model for splitting without explicit matrix formation or factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a conic splitting method that accesses a linear map \(A\) only through products \(v\mapsto Av\) and \(y\mapsto A^*y\), and solves each affine subproblem by an iterative method using at most \(t_k\) such products. If one product costs \(C_{\mathrm{mv}}\), cone processing costs \(C_K\), and vector storage has dimension \(d\), then iteration \(k\) costs \[O(t_kC_{\mathrm{mv}}+C_K+d)\] and requires \(O(M_A+M_K+d)\) storage, where \(M_A\) and \(M_K\) are operator and cone workspace requirements. No dense factorization cost or factor storage is incurred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free solver replaces factorization by repeated operator products, with work proportional to inner iterations and storage proportional to operator and cone workspaces.
assumptions_latex: Both \(A\) and \(A^*\) are available as matrix-vector oracles.
The affine subproblem is solved iteratively.
No explicit dense matrix or factor is stored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iteration \(k\) uses \(O(t_kC_{\mathrm{mv}}+C_K+d)\) work and \(O(M_A+M_K+d)\) storage.

notation.meaning: Number of operator products used by the inner solve.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Accuracy Tail Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case finite-precision certification boundary for a persistently perturbed local contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a computed nonnegative residual satisfy \[\widehat r_{k+1}\leq\rho\widehat r_k+\delta,\] where \(0<\rho<1\) and \(\delta\geq0\) uniformly bounds persistent affine-solve, projection, and floating-point perturbations. Then \[\widehat r_k\leq\rho^k\widehat r_0+\frac{\delta(1-\rho^k)}{1-\rho},\qquad \limsup_{k\to\infty}\widehat r_k\leq\frac{\delta}{1-\rho}.\] Thus \(\delta/(1-\rho)\) is a worst-case asymptotic certification threshold for this recurrence, not a lower bound on every realized residual. A uniform guarantee below that threshold requires a smaller perturbation bound or additional algorithm-specific information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent numerical error gives a worst-case residual neighborhood for the contraction model. The recurrence alone cannot uniformly guarantee tolerances below its asymptotic threshold, although a particular run may attain a smaller residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat r_k\geq0\) for every \(k\).
The additive perturbation contribution is uniformly bounded by \(\delta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\widehat r_k\leq\delta/(1-\rho)\), and the recurrence alone supplies no uniform guarantee below this threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and normalized feasibility diagnostics for equality-form conic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic primal problem \[\text{minimize }\langle c,x\rangle\quad\text{subject to }Ax=b,\quad x\in K,\] define the equality-feasibility residual and cone-feasibility residual by \[r_{\mathrm{eq}}(x)=\lVert Ax-b\rVert,\qquad r_K(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,K).\] A combined absolute primal residual is \(r_p(x)=\max\{r_{\mathrm{eq}}(x),r_K(x)\}\). With a fixed norm and scale floor \(\tau>0\), a normalized diagnostic is \[\widehat r_p(x)=\max\left\{\frac{\lVert Ax-b\rVert}{\max\{\tau,\lVert b\rVert\}},\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,K)}{\max\{\tau,\lVert x\rVert\}}\right\}.\] Both residuals vanish exactly at primal-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility is measured by equality violation and distance to the cone, optionally normalized by fixed data and iterate scales.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(A\) is linear and all norms are fixed.
\(\tau>0\) is a prescribed scale floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_p(x)=0\) if and only if \(Ax=b\) and \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Feasibility Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the minimization-form conic primal-dual convention stated in the assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For conic data \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and a candidate dual vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), define the dual feasibility residual vector and its norm by \[r_d:=A^{\mathsf T}y+c,\qquad \rho_d:=\lVert r_d\rVert.\] Thus \(\rho_d\geq 0\), and \(r_d=0\), equivalently \(\rho_d=0\), exactly when \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\). Membership of \(y\) in \(K^*\) is a separate cone-membership diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual feasibility residual vector is the stationarity defect, and its scalar magnitude is the norm of that defect. Both vanish exactly when the dual stationarity equation is satisfied.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is a closed convex cone.
The primal-dual convention is \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\), and \(y\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_d=0\), equivalently \(\rho_d=0\), if and only if the dual stationarity equation holds exactly.

notation.meaning: norm of the dual feasibility residual vector

Hence \(\rho_g=0\) precisely when those objective values agree.

children.title: Complementarity–Gap Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks between complementarity evidence and gap evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity–Gap Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic consistency identity, including infeasible candidate iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For every candidate triple \((x,s,y)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^m\), the objective gap, complementarity, and affine residuals satisfy \[r_g=\langle s,y\rangle+\langle x,r_d\rangle-\langle y,r_p\rangle.\] Consequently, when \(r_p=0\) and \(r_d=0\), the signed objective gap equals the complementarity residual: \(r_g=\langle s,y\rangle\). For inexact candidates, the displayed correction terms quantify their discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every compatible candidate triple, the signed objective gap equals complementarity plus explicit dual- and primal-feasibility correction terms.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
Residuals use \(r_p:=Ax+s-b\) and \(r_d:=A^{\mathsf T}y+c\).
The signed objective gap is \(r_g:=c^{\mathsf T}x+b^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_g-\langle s,y\rangle=\langle x,r_d\rangle-\langle y,r_p\rangle\).

children.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence derived from fixed-point maps used by splitting solvers.

assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is the fixed-point operator used by the solver on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{fp}}(z)=0\) if and only if \(z\) is a fixed point of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-level definition independent of a particular splitting implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an iterate \(z\in H\), define the fixed-point residual vector and scalar diagnostic by \[r_{\mathrm{fp}}(z):=z-Tz,\qquad \rho_{\mathrm{fp}}(z):=\lVert z-Tz\rVert_H.\] The scalar is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \(z=Tz\). If the implementation reports successive iterates with \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), then \(r_{\mathrm{fp}}(z^k)=z^k-z^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-point residual measures the difference between an iterate and one application of the solver operator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract fixed-point definition is mathematically sound, but this solver-diagnostic leaf requires evidence identifying the relevant solver operator and interface convention.

children.title: Embedding Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence derived from homogeneous or extended embedding variables.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\to V\) is the residual map defining the solver's embedding equations.
\(U\) and \(V\) are finite-dimensional normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{emb}}(u)=0\) if and only if \(u\) solves the embedding equations \(F(u)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract residual for whichever homogeneous or primal-dual embedding the solver exposes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an embedding candidate \(u\in U\), define \[r_{\mathrm{emb}}(u):=F(u),\qquad \rho_{\mathrm{emb}}(u):=\lVert F(u)\rVert_V.\] If the embedding equations have block form \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_q)\), the interface may additionally report \(\lVert F_i(u)\rVert\) for each block. The aggregate residual vanishes exactly on the embedding solution set \(F^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An embedding residual is the norm of the equation defect for the solver's chosen conic embedding.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic norm-of-defect definition is valid, but no source identifies the conic embedding, its equation map, or the residual blocks exposed by the intended interface.

children.title: Fixed-Point-to-Embedding Residual Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between fixed-point residual measures and embedding residual measures.

assumptions_latex: \(R:Z\to U\) recovers an embedding variable from a fixed-point iterate.
There is a linear map \(M:Z\to V\) satisfying \(F(Rz)=M(z-Tz)\) for every \(z\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{emb}}(Rz)=M r_{\mathrm{fp}}(z)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{emb}}(Rz)\leq\lVert M\rVert\rho_{\mathrm{fp}}(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional transfer identity for a solver whose recovery map satisfies the stated factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(r_{\mathrm{fp}}(z):=z-Tz\) and \(r_{\mathrm{emb}}(u):=F(u)\), the assumed factorization gives \[r_{\mathrm{emb}}(Rz)=M r_{\mathrm{fp}}(z).\] Therefore \[\rho_{\mathrm{emb}}(Rz)\leq \lVert M\rVert\rho_{\mathrm{fp}}(z).\] If \(M\) is bounded below by \(\alpha>0\), meaning \(\lVert Mw\rVert\,\geq\alpha\lVert w\rVert\), then also \(\alpha\rho_{\mathrm{fp}}(z)\leq\rho_{\mathrm{emb}}(Rz)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual transfer map converts fixed-point defects into embedding defects and yields norm comparison bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point-to-Embedding Residual Mapping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conclusions follow conditionally from the assumed factorization, but that factorization is the substantive solver-specific mapping and has no supporting source. An actual embedding and recovery construction must be cited.

children.title: Absolute Residual Scales
children.top_down_role: Residual interpretation using fixed problem-independent magnitude thresholds.

assumptions_latex: \(R:X\to Y\) is a residual map between finite-dimensional normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{abs}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(R(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unnormalized residual magnitude in the units of the residual equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate \(x\in X\), the absolute residual scale associated with \(R\) is \[\rho_{\mathrm{abs}}(x):=\lVert R(x)\rVert_Y.\] An absolute stopping test has the form \(\rho_{\mathrm{abs}}(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\), where \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\geq0\) has the same units as \(R(x)\). This scale is not invariant under multiplication of the residual equation by a nonzero scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolute residual is the unnormalized norm of an equation defect, compared with a tolerance in the same units.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Residual Scales

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic absolute-residual definition is coherent and fits the leaf, but the diagnostic norm and stopping convention require an inspectable solver or numerical-optimization source.

children.title: Relative Residual Scales
children.top_down_role: Residual interpretation normalized by problem data or iterate magnitudes.

assumptions_latex: \(R:X\to Y\) is a residual map.
\(S:X\to[0,\infty)\) is a problem-dependent reference magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{rel}}(x)=\lVert R(x)\rVert_Y/S(x)\) whenever \(S(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless normalization by an explicitly chosen nonzero reference magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a candidate \(x\in X\) for which \(S(x)>0\), define the relative residual scale by \[\rho_{\mathrm{rel}}(x):=\frac{\lVert R(x)\rVert_Y}{S(x)}.\] A relative stopping test is \(\rho_{\mathrm{rel}}(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\). The reference \(S(x)\) must be reported with the diagnostic; without it, relative residual values from different interfaces need not be comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative residual divides the defect norm by a stated nonzero reference magnitude, producing a dimensionless diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Residual Scales

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is correct for positive S(x), but the choice of reference magnitude and the interface policy at zero scale are solver-specific and unsupported.

children.title: Mixed Residual Scales
children.top_down_role: Residual interpretation combining absolute floors with relative normalization.

assumptions_latex: \(R:X\to Y\) is a residual map.
\(S:X\to[0,\infty)\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\geq0\), and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed test is \(\lVert R(x)\rVert_Y\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}S(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined absolute-relative stopping rule with an explicit reference scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A candidate \(x\in X\) satisfies the mixed residual criterion when \[\lVert R(x)\rVert_Y\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}S(x).\] The absolute term controls behavior when \(S(x)\) is small or zero, while the relative term scales with problem magnitude. Equivalently, if the denominator is positive, the normalized mixed residual \[\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(x):=\frac{\lVert R(x)\rVert_Y}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}S(x)}\] must not exceed \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed criterion accepts a residual below an absolute tolerance plus a relative tolerance times a reference magnitude.

children.title: Scaled-Coordinate Residuals

assumptions_latex: The original affine residual is \(r:=Ax+s-b\).
\(D\) and \(E\) are invertible coordinate scalings with \(x=D\widehat{x}\), \(s=E^{-1}\widehat{s}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat r=Er\), so scaled and original residuals vanish simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine residual under invertible primal and constraint coordinate scalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define scaled data by \(\widehat A:=EAD\) and \(\widehat b:=Eb\). For scaled variables \(\widehat x:=D^{-1}x\) and \(\widehat s:=Es\), the scaled-coordinate residual is \[\widehat r:=\widehat A\widehat x+\widehat s-\widehat b=E(Ax+s-b)=Er.\] Hence \(\widehat r=0\) if and only if \(r=0\). Moreover, \(\lVert\widehat r\rVert\leq\lVert E\rVert\lVert r\rVert\), so its numerical magnitude depends on the constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under invertible coordinate scaling, the scaled affine residual equals the original residual multiplied by the constraint scaling matrix.

children.title: Original-Coordinate Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residuals mapped back to the user problem's coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Coordinate Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual tuple for a primal-dual conic iterate in the user’s unscaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal problem 
\(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and dual problem \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), define the original-coordinate residuals of \(z=(x,y,s)\) by
\[
r_p=Ax-b,\qquad r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c,\qquad r_g=c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y,
\]
and the cone violations by \(r_K=\operatorname{dist}(x,K)\) and \(r_{K^*}=\operatorname{dist}(s,K^*)\). The diagnostic residual tuple is \(R_{\mathrm{orig}}(z)=(r_p,r_d,r_g,r_K,r_{K^*})\), evaluated using the original data, units, and chosen norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Original-coordinate residuals measure primal equality, dual equality, objective-gap, and cone violations using the unscaled problem data and variables.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{orig}}(z)=(Ax-b,\ A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c,\ c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,K),\ \operatorname{dist}(s,K^*))\).
review_flags: Exact solver-interface convention and supporting locator are not supplied.

children.title: Residual Unscaling Distortion
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic distortion arising when scaling transformations strongly amplify residual components.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Unscaling Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies norm distortion when a scaled residual is returned to original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the scaled and original residual vectors satisfy \(\widetilde r=S r\), where \(S\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) is invertible. Then \(r=S^{-1}\widetilde r\), and every induced norm obeys
\[
\frac{1}{\lVert S\rVert}\lVert\widetilde r\rVert
\le \lVert r\rVert
\le \lVert S^{-1}\rVert\lVert\widetilde r\rVert.
\]
Consequently, the ratio between the largest possible and smallest possible unscaling amplification is at most \(\kappa(S)=\lVert S\rVert\lVert S^{-1}\rVert\). For diagonal \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_i)\) in the Euclidean norm, individual residual components are amplified by \(1/|s_i|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unscaling can amplify residuals by the inverse scaling norm, with directional variation controlled by the scaling condition number.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is invertible.
\(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is a vector norm and its induced matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert S\rVert^{-1}\lVert\widetilde r\rVert\le\lVert S^{-1}\widetilde r\rVert\le\lVert S^{-1}\rVert\lVert\widetilde r\rVert\).

notation.meaning: Condition number in the selected induced norm.

review_flags: Standard norm inequality, but no directly relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The norm inequalities are correct under the stated induced-norm convention, and the property fits the Residual Unscaling Distortion leaf. No source or locator is supplied for the claimed diagnostic interpretation or scaling-distortion convention.

children.title: Normwise Errors
children.top_down_role: Aggregate error measures based on vector or operator norms.

knowledge_statements.title: Normwise Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global residual error normalized by a single aggregate scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\in\mathbb R^q\) be a residual vector and let \(\sigma>0\) be a prescribed global scale derived from the problem data and candidate iterate. The normwise relative error is
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{norm}}(r;\sigma)=\frac{\lVert r\rVert}{\sigma}.
\]
A regularized convention may set \(\sigma=\tau+\sigma_0\), where \(\tau>0\) and \(\sigma_0\ge0\) is the natural data scale. A tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is satisfied normwise exactly when \(\lVert r\rVert\le\varepsilon\sigma\). The norm and construction of \(\sigma\) are part of the diagnostic specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normwise error divides the norm of the entire residual vector by one declared global problem scale.
assumptions_latex: \(r\in\mathbb R^q\).
\(\sigma>0\) is fixed by the diagnostic convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{\mathrm{norm}}(r;\sigma)=\lVert r\rVert/\sigma\).
review_flags: Normalization conventions vary across solvers; no diagnostic source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a precise definition of one possible normwise diagnostic and the definition content kind fits the leaf. The construction of the aggregate scale is convention-dependent, and the record supplies neither a source locator nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Componentwise Errors
children.top_down_role: Error measures retaining coordinate-level or block-level variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual error normalized separately in each coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\in\mathbb R^q\) and let \(d\in\mathbb R_+^q\) contain prescribed coordinate scales. Define the componentwise relative error by
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{comp}}(r;d)=\max_{1\le i\le q}\frac{|r_i|}{d_i},
\]
using the extended-value convention \(|r_i|/0=0\) when \(r_i=0\), and \(|r_i|/0=+\infty\) otherwise. Equivalently, \(\eta_{\mathrm{comp}}(r;d)\le\varepsilon\) exactly when \(|r_i|\le\varepsilon d_i\) for every coordinate \(i\). Positive regularizers may be added to \(d_i\) when zero scales are not intended to impose exact equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A componentwise error compares each residual coordinate with its own scale and reports the worst relative violation.
assumptions_latex: \(r\in\mathbb R^q\).
\(d\in\mathbb R_+^q\) is fixed by the diagnostic convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{\mathrm{comp}}(r;d)=\max_i |r_i|/d_i\) under the stated zero-denominator convention.

notation.meaning: Scale assigned to residual coordinate i.

review_flags: Component scaling is interface-dependent; no directly supporting locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinatewise maximum and zero-denominator convention are internally consistent, and the definition content kind fits the leaf. The scale construction and regularization convention require a supporting diagnostic or numerical-analysis source with a specific locator.

children.title: Normwise–Componentwise Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Cases where aggregate accuracy obscures large localized errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Normwise–Componentwise Disagreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A small normwise residual need not imply small componentwise relative error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q\ge2\), choose \(0<\delta<1\), \(d=(\delta,1,\ldots,1)\), and \(r=(\delta,0,\ldots,0)\). With Euclidean global scale \(\sigma=\lVert d\rVert_2\),
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{norm}}(r;\sigma)=\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{q-1+\delta^2}},
\qquad
\eta_{\mathrm{comp}}(r;d)=1.
\]
Thus the normwise error tends to zero as \(\delta\downarrow0\), while the componentwise error remains one. Aggregate normalization can therefore conceal a full relative violation in a coordinate whose natural scale is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual confined to a tiny-scale coordinate can look negligible normwise while remaining a 100-percent componentwise error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{\mathrm{norm}}\to0\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), but \(\eta_{\mathrm{comp}}=1\).

notation.meaning: Small scale of the first coordinate.

review_flags: Explicit construction is checkable, but a source for the intended diagnostic interpretation is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed construction correctly separates the stated normwise and componentwise diagnostics, and counterexample is the appropriate content kind for this terminal container. The record lacks a cited source or explicit standard-field rationale for retaining the construction as candidate knowledge.

children.title: Forward Error
children.top_down_role: Accuracy of computed solutions relative to reference solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Forward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance from a reported conic iterate to the exact solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For conic problem data \(d=(A,b,c,K)\), let \(\mathcal S(d)\) denote the set of primal-dual solutions satisfying primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and zero duality gap. Given a reported iterate \(\widehat z\) and a norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_Z\) on the product variable space, its absolute forward error is
\[
e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat z;d)=\operatorname{dist}_Z(\widehat z,\mathcal S(d))
=\inf_{z^\star\in\mathcal S(d)}\lVert\widehat z-z^\star\rVert_Z.
\]
If \(\mathcal S(d)=\varnothing\), set \(e_{\mathrm f}=+\infty\). A relative version divides by a declared positive solution scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward error is the distance from the computed primal-dual iterate to the exact solution set of the original problem.
assumptions_latex: A norm on the primal-dual product space is fixed.
\(\mathcal S(d)\) is the exact solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat z;d)=\inf_{z^\star\in\mathcal S(d)}\lVert\widehat z-z^\star\rVert_Z\).
review_flags: No supplied locator addresses forward error for conic solver diagnostics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Distance to the exact solution set is a standard and precise forward-error definition, and the content kind matches the leaf. No authoritative source with a section, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Backward Error
children.top_down_role: Perturbation-based accuracy of computed solutions relative to nearby cone programs.

knowledge_statements.title: Backward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smallest admissible data perturbation making a reported iterate exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d\) be conic problem data, let \(\widehat z\) be a reported primal-dual iterate, and let \(\mathcal P\) be a declared class of admissible perturbations that preserves dimensions and cone representation. For a data norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_D\), define the absolute backward error by
\[
e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat z;d)=
\inf\bigl\{\lVert\Delta d\rVert_D:\Delta d\in\mathcal P,\ \widehat z\in\mathcal S(d+\Delta d)\bigr\}.
\]
The infimum is \(+\infty\) if no admissible perturbation makes \(\widehat z\) exact. A relative backward error divides by a specified positive scale for \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward error is the smallest allowed perturbation of the problem data under which the reported iterate becomes an exact solution.
assumptions_latex: A data norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_D\) is fixed.
The admissible perturbation class \(\mathcal P\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat z;d)=\inf\{\lVert\Delta d\rVert_D:\Delta d\in\mathcal P,\ \widehat z\in\mathcal S(d+\Delta d)\}\).
review_flags: Admissible perturbations are solver-interface dependent; no relevant locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly makes backward error depend on a declared perturbation class and data norm, and it fits the leaf. Because those choices materially determine the quantity, an inspectable source locator or explicit standard-field rationale is required.

children.title: Forward–Backward Error Separation
children.top_down_role: Conditioning regimes where small backward error coexists with substantial forward error.

knowledge_statements.title: Forward–Backward Error Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small backward error does not uniformly control forward error near ill-conditioned problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the scalar equation \(a x=b\) with \(a=b=\varepsilon>0\) and reported value \(\widehat x=0\). Its exact solution is \(x^\star=1\), so the absolute forward error is \(1\). If only the right-hand side may be perturbed, changing \(b\) to \(b+\Delta b=0\) makes \(\widehat x\) exact with \(|\Delta b|=\varepsilon\); hence the absolute backward error is \(\varepsilon\). Therefore
\[
\frac{e_{\mathrm f}}{e_{\mathrm b}}=\frac1\varepsilon\to+\infty.
\]
A uniform forward-from-backward bound requires an additional conditioning or metric-regularity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ill-conditioning permits arbitrarily small backward error alongside order-one forward error, so residual accuracy alone cannot guarantee solution accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
Only perturbations of the scalar right-hand side are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm f}=1\), \(e_{\mathrm b}=\varepsilon\), and \(e_{\mathrm f}/e_{\mathrm b}\to+\infty\).
review_flags: Explicit example is checkable, but no source locator for the conditioning conclusion was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar example correctly demonstrates unbounded separation between the specified absolute forward and backward errors, and failure_boundary is the appropriate role for the leaf. The conditioning interpretation has no supporting source locator or explicit standard-field rationale.

notation.meaning: Natural scale of the problem data.

review_flags: A source locator is still required for the selected regularization convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward error normalized by a data scale protected against zero or tiny denominators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat z;d)\) be an absolute backward error, let \(s_D(d)\ge 0\) be a prescribed data scale, and choose \(\tau>0\). Define the regularized relative backward error by
\[
\eta_{\mathrm b,\tau}(\widehat z;d)=\frac{e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat z;d)}{s_D(d)+\tau}.
\]
For every tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), one has \(\eta_{\mathrm b,\tau}(\widehat z;d)\le\varepsilon\) if and only if \(e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat z;d)\le\varepsilon(s_D(d)+\tau)\). The positive parameter \(\tau\) prevents a zero denominator and limits sensitivity when the natural scale is very small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized backward error divides the smallest exactifying data perturbation by a data scale plus a positive floor; meeting a tolerance is equivalent to the backward error being no larger than that tolerance times the regularized scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Backward Error
Canonicalization Residual Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pulls canonical-form residuals back to residuals of the modeled problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let original variables and canonical variables be related by \(z=T u+t\), and suppose the canonicalization records an affine residual identity
\[
G(u)=L F(Tu+t),
\]
where \(F(z)=0\) is the original optimality system and \(G(u)=0\) its canonical counterpart. If \(L\) is injective, then canonical exactness is equivalent to original exactness. If \(L\) is invertible, the residuals correspond by
\[
r_{\mathrm{can}}=Lr_{\mathrm{orig}},\qquad
r_{\mathrm{orig}}=L^{-1}r_{\mathrm{can}}.
\]
For an approximate canonical iterate, reconstruction must also report violations of auxiliary equalities not represented in the range of this identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recorded affine map converts original optimality residuals to canonical residuals; invertibility permits exact residual recovery in both directions.
assumptions_latex: The canonicalization supplies affine maps \(T,t,L\).
The residual identity holds on the reconstructed variable domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{can}}=Lr_{\mathrm{orig}}\), and if \(L\) is invertible then \(r_{\mathrm{orig}}=L^{-1}r_{\mathrm{can}}\).
review_flags: Canonicalization maps are implementation-specific, and no applicable source locator was supplied.

Canonicalization and omitted auxiliary-equality handling are implementation-specific, so an applicable source with a precise locator is necessary.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Certificate Branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic alternative certificate recovered from the primal-infeasible homogeneous self-dual branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal conic feasibility system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), a vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is a strict primal-infeasibility certificate when
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.
\]
These conditions are directly verifiable and exclude every primal feasible \(x\), because feasibility would imply \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle A^{\mathsf T}y,x\rangle\ge0\). A homogeneous self-dual iterate on this branch must be rescaled, when its relevant homogeneous scalar is positive, to produce such a \(y\); the recovered certificate should then be checked in the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-infeasible branch returns a vector whose dual-cone membership and negative pairing with the right-hand side certify primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
The recovered vector satisfies the displayed strict inequalities in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) certify that \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Infeasibility Certificate Branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic recession certificate recovered from the dual-infeasible homogeneous self-dual branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair with primal objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), a vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) is a strict dual-infeasibility certificate when
\[
d\in K,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.
\]
These conditions are directly verifiable. They exclude dual feasibility: if \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\) with \(s\in K^*\), then \(c^{\mathsf T}d=y^{\mathsf T}Ad+s^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\), contradicting the strict inequality. When a primal feasible point exists, \(d\) is also a recession direction proving primal unboundedness. The homogeneous self-dual branch must be normalized and checked in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual-infeasible branch returns a cone recession direction annihilated by the constraints and having strictly negative objective slope.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
The recovered direction satisfies the displayed conditions in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in K\), \(Ad=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) certify dual infeasibility; with primal feasibility they also certify primal unboundedness.

children.title: Certificate Normalization
children.top_down_role: Scale conventions used to present homogeneous infeasibility certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical scaling of homogeneous primal- or dual-infeasibility rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the conic pair 
\[\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\qquad \max\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\},\]
a nonzero primal improving ray \(x\) satisfying \(x\in K\), \(Ax=0\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle<0\) is normalized as \(\widehat x=x/(-\langle c,x\rangle)\). A dual improving ray \((y,s)\) satisfying \(s\in K^*\), \(A^*y+s=0\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\) is normalized as \((\widehat y,\widehat s)=(y,s)/\langle b,y\rangle\). Thus \(\langle c,\widehat x\rangle=-1\) or \(\langle b,\widehat y\rangle=1\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale an infeasibility ray by its nonzero separating objective so that the resulting certificate has unit margin.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(A\) is linear and \(K^*\) is the dual cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle c,\widehat x\rangle=-1\) or \(\langle b,\widehat y\rangle=1\), with all cone and homogeneous equations preserved.

children.title: Certificate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Mapping embedding-space certificate information to the original cone program.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of an original-space certificate from a homogeneous embedding iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an embedding output \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) and tolerances \(\epsilon_{\rm emb},\epsilon_{\rm cert}>0\). First require \(\tau\leq\epsilon_{\rm emb}\), \(\kappa>\epsilon_{\rm emb}\), and acceptably small embedding residuals. If \(x\in K\), \(\|Ax\|\leq\epsilon_{\rm cert}\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle<0\), output \(\widehat x=x/(-\langle c,x\rangle)\). Otherwise, if \(s\in K^*\), \(\|A^*y+s\|\leq\epsilon_{\rm cert}\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\), output \((\widehat y,\widehat s)=(y,s)/\langle b,y\rangle\). If neither branch passes, output no certificate rather than assigning an infeasibility status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test the embedding output against primal and dual ray equations, normalize the passing branch, and otherwise report no certificate.
assumptions_latex: The embedding uses the conic-pair sign convention stated in Certificate Normalization.
Cone membership and residual norms can be evaluated to the requested tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned output is a normalized approximate improving-ray certificate for the original conic pair.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the recovery leaf, but the cited embedding section does not yet establish this particular tolerance-based procedure. Absolute residual tests performed before normalization do not by themselves control the residuals of the normalized output when the certificate margin is small. A source or precise scale-aware validation rule is required before the mathematical reliability of the recovery algorithm can be assessed.

children.title: Normalization-Sensitive Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery sensitivity caused by small normalization denominators or extreme certificate scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization-Sensitive Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical reliability boundary for division by a small certificate margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\) be a computed ray candidate, let \(m(z)=-\langle c,z\rangle\) for a primal ray or \(m(z)=\langle b,y\rangle\) for a dual ray, and suppose \(m(z)>0\). Normalization maps \(z\) to \(z/m(z)\); hence an absolute perturbation \(\delta z\) can be amplified on the order of \(1/m(z)\), with additional sensitivity from perturbing \(m(z)\). Recovery is therefore rejected when \(m(z)\leq\epsilon_{\rm scale}\|z\|\), even if homogeneous residuals are small. Passing this test does not itself certify validity: the normalized cone, equation, and sign residuals must still pass independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tiny separating margin makes normalization unstable, so recovery must reject poorly scaled rays and recheck normalized residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(z\neq0\) is represented in a fixed norm.
\(\epsilon_{\rm scale}>0\) is a prescribed scale-safety threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(z)\leq\epsilon_{\rm scale}\|z\|\) is a failure boundary for numerically reliable normalization-based recovery.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, and small normalization margins are genuinely ill-conditioned. However, the prescribed rejection threshold is solver-dependent and is not supported by the cited embedding locator. The informal amplification statement also omits the dependence on perturbations of the margin and the norm of the ray, so authoritative numerical-analysis or solver-interface support is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Improving Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-direction certificate of primal objective decrease and dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\). A primal improving ray is a vector \(d\) satisfying
\[d\in K,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad \langle c,d\rangle<0.\]
If the primal problem has a feasible point \(x_0\), then \(x_0+t d\) is feasible for every \(t\geq0\) and its objective tends to \(-\infty\). Independently of primal feasibility, such a ray excludes feasibility of the dual system \(A^*y+s=c\), \(s\in K^*\), because dual feasibility would imply \(\langle c,d\rangle=\langle s,d\rangle\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone recession direction with zero constraint displacement and negative cost certifies dual infeasibility and, when primal feasibility exists, primal unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The primal and dual use finite-dimensional adjoint pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\) certifies dual infeasibility; if the primal is feasible, its optimal value is \(-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Improving Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual recession-direction certificate of primal infeasibility and dual objective increase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual problem \(\max\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), a dual improving ray is a pair \((d_y,d_s)\) satisfying
\[d_s\in K^*,\qquad A^*d_y+d_s=0,\qquad \langle b,d_y\rangle>0.\]
If \((y_0,s_0)\) is dual feasible, then \((y_0+t d_y,s_0+t d_s)\) is feasible for every \(t\geq0\), and its objective tends to \(+\infty\). Independently of dual feasibility, the ray excludes primal feasibility: any \(x\in K\) with \(Ax=b\) would give \(\langle b,d_y\rangle=-\langle x,d_s\rangle\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual recession direction with positive objective slope certifies primal infeasibility and, when dual feasibility exists, dual unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The primal and dual use finite-dimensional adjoint pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((d_y,d_s)\) certifies primal infeasibility; if the dual is feasible, its optimal value is \(+\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Bearing Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-scale homogeneous-embedding outcome yielding primal-dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) solve a homogeneous self-dual embedding whose original variables are recovered by division by \(\tau\). The outcome is solution-bearing when \(\tau>0\) and \(\kappa=0\). Then
\[\bar x=x/\tau,\qquad \bar y=y/\tau,\qquad \bar s=s/\tau\]
satisfy \(A\bar x=b\), \(A^*\bar y+\bar s=c\), \(\bar x\in K\), and \(\bar s\in K^*\). The embedding gap identity yields \(\langle c,\bar x\rangle=\langle b,\bar y\rangle\); hence the recovered points are primal and dual optimal whenever the embedding equations hold exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An embedding solution with positive solution scale and zero certificate scale recovers a primal-dual optimal pair by division by the solution scale.
assumptions_latex: The embedding has the stated recovery convention and exact residual equations.
\(K\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) is a primal-dual feasible zero-gap solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Bearing Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-solution-scale embedding outcome yielding an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\neq0\) satisfy a homogeneous self-dual embedding for the stated primal-dual pair. The outcome is certificate-bearing when \(\tau=0\), \(\kappa>0\), and at least one strict certificate margin is present. If \(x\in K\), \(Ax=0\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle<0\), then \(x\) is a primal improving ray. If \(s\in K^*\), \(A^*y+s=0\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\), then \((y,s)\) is a dual improving ray. Each passing branch is normalized by its strict margin before being returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero solution scale and positive certificate scale, a valid strict-margin ray yields an original primal- or dual-infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The embedding output satisfies its homogeneous equations exactly.
The primal-dual sign convention matches the displayed ray tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A passing branch yields a normalized certificate of dual or primal infeasibility, respectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate embedding directions that expose a proper cone face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an embedding limit has \(\tau=\kappa=0\) and produces a nonzero vector \(w\in K^*\) satisfying \(A^*y+w=0\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle=0\). Then every primal feasible \(x\in K\) obeys \(\langle w,x\rangle=0\), so feasibility is confined to the exposed face
\[F=K\cap w^\perp.\]
If \(F\subsetneq K\), the pair \((y,w)\) is a facial-reduction certificate rather than a strict infeasibility certificate. The original conic system may be reformulated over \(F\); no claim of infeasibility follows solely from this zero-margin direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero zero-margin dual direction can expose a proper face containing every feasible point, calling for facial reduction rather than infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The displayed embedding direction satisfies its equations exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=K\cap w^\perp\) contains the primal feasible set, and \(F\subsetneq K\) certifies a valid facial reduction.

notation.meaning: exposed face containing the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Indeterminate Embedding Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding outputs insufficient for either solution or certificate recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An embedding output is indeterminate when no validated classification predicate holds: it has neither \(\tau>\epsilon_\tau\) with recoverable primal-dual residuals, nor \(\kappa>\epsilon_\kappa\) with a strict normalized improving-ray margin, nor a verified nonzero facial-reduction direction. In particular, \(\tau\leq\epsilon_\tau\) and \(\kappa\leq\epsilon_\kappa\), large embedding residuals, or normalization margins below the scale threshold prevent a mathematical status claim. The diagnostic must return an indeterminate or inaccurate status together with residuals and scales; it must not infer feasibility, infeasibility, or unboundedness from scalar signs alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If no solution, strict certificate, or facial-reduction test passes, the embedding outcome is indeterminate and supports no problem-status claim.
assumptions_latex: \(\epsilon_\tau,\epsilon_\kappa>0\) are declared numerical tolerances.
All classification branches include independent residual validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of every validated branch requires an indeterminate status, not a feasibility or infeasibility conclusion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf and the conservative no-status conclusion is mathematically sensible. However, the exact disjunction of tolerance-based predicates, the inaccurate-status behavior, and the required diagnostic payload are solver-interface rules not established by the cited general embedding locator. A solver-specific authoritative source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Infimal-Displacement-Vector Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point displacement representation used to diagnose inconsistent splitting problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:H\to H\) be a firmly nonexpansive fixed-point operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and define its infimal displacement vector by
\[v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0).\]
For the iteration \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), the displacement sequence \(z^k-z^{k+1}\) converges to \(v\). Thus \(v=0\) is compatible with asymptotic regularity, whereas \(v\neq0\) detects absence of fixed points whenever \(0\notin\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}\). In a conic splitting solver, only a separately established problem-specific map from components of \(v\) to conic ray equations turns this diagnostic into an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum-norm fixed-point displacement is the limit of successive-iterate differences; a solver-specific mapping is required to turn it into a conic certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite-dimensional and \(T\) is firmly nonexpansive.
The fixed-point iteration is well defined for every \(k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^k-z^{k+1}\to v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the nontrivial convergence assertion for firmly nonexpansive iterations. Moreover, the statement's principal mathematical role is a convergence property or theorem rather than merely a representation. An authoritative fixed-point source with a theorem or page locator is required before the precise hypotheses and content kind can be settled.

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Iterates Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate extraction from limiting differences of fixed-point iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) and \(d^k=z^k-z^{k+1}\). Suppose \(d^k\to d\), and a solver-specific linear recovery map \(R\) produces \(R(d)=(x,y,s)\). The limiting difference is a primal certificate if \(x\in K\), \(Ax=0\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle<0\); it is a dual certificate if \(s\in K^*\), \(A^*y+s=0\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\). A finite iterate \(d^k\) is reported only after the corresponding cone, homogeneous-equation, and strict-margin residuals pass declared tolerances, followed by normalization of the passing margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map a converged iterate difference into conic variables, validate the ray equations and strict margin, then normalize the resulting certificate.
assumptions_latex: The difference sequence converges.
The recovery map \(R\) is derived for the particular splitting formulation.
Cone and equation residuals are computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A validated passing branch of \(R(d)\) is an improving-ray infeasibility certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ray-validation tests are sufficient once a recovered limit is available, and the certificate kind fits the leaf. However, no source establishes convergence of the iterate differences or a concrete recovery map for any specified splitting formulation. Without that information, the claimed certificate-extraction method is not independently assessable.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized-Iterate Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic ray extraction from diverging fixed-point iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) be a solver iteration with \(\|z^k\|\to\infty\), and let \(u\) be a nonzero cluster point of \(u^k=z^k/\|z^k\|\). Given a solver-specific homogeneous recovery map \(R\), write \(R(u)=(x,y,s)\). The direction yields a primal certificate only if \(x\in K\), \(Ax=0\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle<0\); it yields a dual certificate only if \(s\in K^*\), \(A^*y+s=0\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\). Normalized iterates alone are not certificates: every recovered cluster direction must pass these equations and a scale-safe strict-margin test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized direction from diverging iterates becomes a certificate only after a solver-specific recovery map and full improving-ray validation.
assumptions_latex: The iterates are unbounded and possess the stated cluster direction.
The map \(R\) respects the homogeneous scaling of the solver variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A recovered direction is reportable exactly when a primal or dual improving-ray validation branch passes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement appropriately refuses to treat a normalized cluster direction as a certificate until the improving-ray equations pass. Nevertheless, no source identifies a solver for which normalized iterates have the required asymptotic interpretation or defines the homogeneous recovery map. Those missing facts are essential to this certificate method.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized-Average Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers scale-independent certificate candidates formed from weighted averages; it does not claim that averaging alone establishes the certificate conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\in\mathbb N\), let \(w_k>0\) for \(k=1,\ldots,N\), and form the weighted averages \(\bar x_N\) and \(\bar y_N\). If \(b^T\bar y_N<0\), \(A^T\bar y_N=0\), and \(\bar y_N\in K^*\), then \(\widehat y_N=\bar y_N/(-b^T\bar y_N)\) satisfies \(A^T\widehat y_N=0\), \(\widehat y_N\in K^*\), and \(b^T\widehat y_N=-1\), so it is a normalized primal-infeasibility certificate. If \(c^T\bar x_N<0\) and \(-A\bar x_N\in K\), then \(\widehat x_N=\bar x_N/(-c^T\bar x_N)\) satisfies \(-A\widehat x_N\in K\) and \(c^T\widehat x_N=-1\), so it is a normalized dual-infeasibility certificate. In the presence of a known primal feasible point, the latter also certifies primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted average becomes a scale-independent infeasibility certificate only when it also satisfies the relevant exact cone, linear, and strict-sign conditions. A normalized primal recession direction proves unboundedness only when primal feasibility is known.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*\).
The conic pair is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}\) and \(\max\{-b^Ty:A^Ty+c=0,\ y\in K^*\}\).
For \(k=1,\ldots,N\), \(x^k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y^k\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(w_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the corresponding cone, linear, and strict-sign conditions, \(\widehat y_N\) or \(\widehat x_N\) is a scale-independent infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: Weighted averages of primal and dual iterates.

notation.symbol_latex: \(\widehat y_N=\bar y_N/(-b^T\bar y_N)\), \(\widehat x_N=\bar x_N/(-c^T\bar x_N)\)
notation.meaning: Normalized averaged certificate candidates when the respective denominators are positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Solution Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States exact conic optimal-solution termination; acceptance relying only on nonzero tolerances belongs to an approximate status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}\) and \(\max\{-b^Ty:A^Ty+c=0,\ y\in K^*\}\), an exact optimal-solution termination status is justified when \(r_p=0\), \(r_d=0\), \(s\in K\), \(y\in K^*\), and \(g=0\). Under these conditions, \(x\) and \(y\) are optimal for their respective problems. If acceptance relies only on nonzero residual or gap tolerances rather than exact validation, the status must be identified as approximate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact optimal termination requires primal and dual feasibility, cone membership, and zero duality gap. A result accepted only through nonzero tolerances must be labeled approximate.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*\).
The reported vectors satisfy \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(s,y\in\mathbb R^m\) and are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact optimal-solution termination predicate is \(r_p=0\), \(r_d=0\), \(s\in K\), \(y\in K^*\), and \(g=0\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the primal slack cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States exact strong-infeasibility termination through a conic alternative certificate; approximate relations do not justify the exact status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver may terminate with exact primal infeasibility when it returns a finite vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(A^Ty=0\), \(y\in K^*\), and \(b^Ty<0\). Positive rescaling preserves these conditions, so the diagnostic interface may equivalently require the normalization \(b^Ty=-1\). Approximate satisfaction of the cone, null-space, or sign conditions does not justify the exact infeasibility status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite dual-cone vector orthogonal to the constraint map and strictly separating the right-hand side certifies exact primal infeasibility; an approximate vector does not justify the exact status.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*\).
The primal constraints are \(Ax+s=b\), where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(s\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of \(y\in K^*\) with \(A^Ty=0\) and \(b^Ty<0\) proves that the primal feasible set is empty.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the slack cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes certified primal unboundedness from a recession direction that, without known primal feasibility, certifies only dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}\), suppose a primal feasible pair \((x_0,s_0)\) is known. A finite vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(-Ad\in K\) and \(c^Td<0\) is then a certificate that the primal optimal value is \(-\infty\), and it justifies primal-unboundedness termination. Without established primal feasibility, the same direction conditions certify dual infeasibility but do not by themselves certify primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A known primal feasible point together with a cone-compatible direction of strictly negative cost certifies primal unboundedness. Without established feasibility, the direction certifies only dual infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a convex cone.
A feasible pair \((x_0,s_0)\in\mathbb R^n\times K\) satisfies \(Ax_0+s_0=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(-Ad\in K\) and \(c^Td<0\), then the primal optimal value is \(-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Known primal feasible point and slack.

children.title: Ambiguous Certificate Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination behavior when numerical evidence cannot reliably distinguish infeasibility from unboundedness.

assumptions_latex: The solver evaluates primal-infeasibility and unboundedness diagnostics using finite tolerances.
Neither exact certificate has been independently validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Simultaneous or nonexclusive approximate acceptance requires an ambiguous-certificate status rather than a definite infeasible or unbounded status.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-tolerance certificate tests may overlap without establishing either exact conic alternative
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies when finite-tolerance diagnostics do not support an exclusive mathematical classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_{\mathrm{inf}}^{\varepsilon}\) denote acceptance of an approximate vector satisfying the primal-infeasibility tests within tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and let \(P_{\mathrm{unb}}^{\varepsilon}\) denote acceptance of an approximate recession direction together with approximate primal feasibility. If both predicates hold, or if numerical uncertainty prevents deciding which predicate is reliable, the solver shall not infer either exact infeasibility or exact unboundedness. It may terminate with an ambiguous-certificate status and report both residual sets, normalization denominators, and \(\varepsilon\). Exact validation of one certificate permits replacement by the corresponding definite status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When finite-tolerance infeasibility and unboundedness tests overlap or cannot be distinguished reliably, terminate as ambiguous and expose both diagnostic residual sets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but overlap handling, required diagnostic fields, and status priority are solver-interface policies. No inspectable source supports the proposed ambiguous-certificate status semantics.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_{\mathrm{sol}}\geq0\) be the maximum of the solver's documented normalized primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, cone-membership, and duality-gap residuals. The status is an accurate solution when \(R_{\mathrm{sol}}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{acc}}\), and an inaccurate solution when \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{acc}}<R_{\mathrm{sol}}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{inacc}}\). If \(R_{\mathrm{sol}}>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{inacc}}\), neither solution status is justified. The returned record must include the component residuals and normalization conventions so that acceptance is independently checkable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to approximate infeasibility or recession certificates after a fixed nonzero normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normalize the nonzero candidate \(q\) by the relevant separating functional or a documented norm, and let \(R_{\mathrm{cert}}(q)\) aggregate its normalized linear-equation, cone-membership, and normalization defects.
