knowledge_statements.title: Small-Separation-Margin Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation boundary for normalized strict-separation certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a conic system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), define the normalized separation margin
\[
\gamma(b)=\sup\{-\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y\in K^*,\ \|y\|\leq1\}.
\]
The support-function bound
\[
|\gamma(b+\Delta b)-\gamma(b)|\leq\|\Delta b\|
\]
holds. Therefore, if \(0<\gamma(b)\leq\tau\), perturbations or numerical uncertainty of size \(\tau\) can eliminate the resolved positive margin, so a tolerance-based interface cannot robustly distinguish strong infeasibility from a zero-margin regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the best normalized separation margin is no larger than data uncertainty, strong-infeasibility classification is not perturbation-robust.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(A\) is linear and Euclidean norms are used.
\(\tau>0\) bounds perturbation or numerical uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\gamma(b)\leq\tau\) places the strong-infeasibility verdict within the perturbation ambiguity band.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: support functions are Lipschitz over a unit-bounded certificate set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized margin and its Lipschitz bound are plausible, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. However, the operational claim that uncertainty of size tau eliminates or makes the margin diagnostically unresolved needs a source specifying the perturbation and interface interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual–Certificate Scale Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of absolute tests on homogeneous certificate rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonzero candidate ray \(y\), define
\[
\rho(y)=\frac{\operatorname{dist}(A^*y,K^*)}{\|y\|},
\qquad
\sigma(y)=\frac{(-\langle b,y\rangle)_+}{{\max\{1,\|b\|\}\|y\|}}.
\]
For every \(\alpha>0\), one has \(\rho(\alpha y)=\rho(y)\) and \(\sigma(\alpha y)=\sigma(y)\), whereas the absolute cone residual and separation value scale by \(\alpha\). Hence a diagnostic combining absolute residual thresholds with an independently scaled certificate threshold can change its verdict along the same ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute residual and certificate tests can disagree because both scale along a ray, while their normalized diagnostic quantities remain invariant.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(y\neq0\) and \(\alpha>0\).
Distances and adjoints use fixed Euclidean inner products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Normalized tests are ray-invariant; unmatched absolute thresholds are not.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive homogeneity of cone distance and linear certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The homogeneity calculations are correct and failure_boundary fits the scale-mismatch leaf, but the conclusion about verdict changes under unmatched solver thresholds is an interface-level diagnostic claim without an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Ray Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued ambiguity of an approximately represented infeasibility ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
\mathcal C=\{y:A^*y\in K^*,\ \langle b,y\rangle<0\}
\]
be the exact strict-certificate set. If a stored vector \(\widehat y\) has a certified error bound \(\|y-\widehat y\|\leq\varepsilon\), it determines a valid certificate only when the entire admissible error set is verified to lie in \(\mathcal C\). Finite-precision ray ambiguity occurs when
\[
B(\widehat y,\varepsilon)\cap\mathcal C\neq\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
B(\widehat y,\varepsilon)\cap\mathcal C^c\neq\varnothing.
\]
Then the stored ray alone does not determine an exact infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rounded ray is ambiguous when its error ball contains both valid strict certificates and invalid vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(\widehat y\) is stored with a valid normwise error bound \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
Certificate predicates are interpreted for the exact data \(A,b,K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the error ball meets both \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal C^c\), certificate validity is unresolved.

notation.meaning: set of exact strict infeasibility certificates
closed error ball around the stored ray

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval-set interpretation of a rounded certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The error-ball formulation is internally coherent and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but the guarantee semantics for a stored finite-precision ray depend on a particular certified-error model that has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Infeasibility Certificate Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of a strict finite-dimensional Farkas certificate in weak infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(b\in\operatorname{cl}A(K)\setminus A(K)\). Then no vector \(y\) can satisfy
\[
A^*y\in K^*,
\qquad
\langle b,y\rangle<0.
\]
Indeed, every \(y\) with \(A^*y\in K^*\) is nonnegative on \(A(K)\), and by continuity it is nonnegative on \(\operatorname{cl}A(K)\), including \(b\). Thus weak infeasibility lacks the ordinary strict separating certificate available for strong infeasibility, even though the primal system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weakly infeasible systems admit no ordinary strict separating dual certificate, leaving a gap between infeasibility and finite Farkas certification.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(A\) is linear between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
\(b\in\operatorname{cl}A(K)\setminus A(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists y\) such that \(A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\).

source_refs.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

source_witnesses.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated absence of a strict separating certificate follows correctly from closure membership, and property fits the leaf. The cited general conic-modeling section is not inspectably shown to support the weak-infeasibility certificate gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Residual Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm distortion caused by invertible row scaling of conic equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the primal residual be \(r_p=Ax-b\), and apply an invertible row scaling \(D\), giving the scaled equation \(D Ax=D b\) and residual \(\widetilde r_p=D r_p\). In Euclidean norm,
\[
\sigma_{\min}(D)\|r_p\|\leq\|\widetilde r_p\|\leq\sigma_{\max}(D)\|r_p\|.
\]
Consequently, a fixed stopping test \(\|\widetilde r_p\|\leq\tau\) corresponds to direction-dependent unscaled tolerances between \(\tau/\sigma_{\max}(D)\) and \(\tau/\sigma_{\min}(D)\), unless residuals are explicitly unscaled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row scaling changes residual norms by the singular values of the scaling matrix, so a fixed scaled tolerance has direction-dependent original meaning.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is invertible.
Residuals use the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\min}(D)\|r_p\|\leq\|D r_p\|\leq\sigma_{\max}(D)\|r_p\|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: singular-value bounds for an invertible linear scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singular-value bounds are correct and property fits the residual-distortion leaf, but the stopping-test interpretation is a solver-diagnostic claim without an inspectable scaling source.

knowledge_statements.title: Badly Balanced Primal–Dual Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware condition detecting asymmetric primal and dual convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair with equations \(Ax=b\) and \(A^*y+s=c\), define
\[
\eta_p=\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|b\|},
\qquad
\eta_d=\frac{\|A^*y+s-c\|}{1+\|c\|}.
\]
Given a prescribed imbalance factor \(\kappa>1\), the residuals are badly balanced when
\[
\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d\}>0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d\}}{\max\{\min\{\eta_p,\eta_d\},\epsilon\}}\geq\kappa,
\]
where \(\epsilon>0\) is the diagnostic floor. A joint stopping rule must therefore report both normalized residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual residuals are badly balanced when their normalized magnitudes differ by at least a prescribed factor above a diagnostic floor.
assumptions_latex: \(x,y,s\) are candidate primal-dual iterates.
\(\kappa>1\) is a prescribed imbalance factor.
\(\epsilon>0\) is a fixed diagnostic floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual-ratio predicate defines bad primal-dual balance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the particular normalizations, diagnostic floor, imbalance ratio, and threshold are interface conventions rather than canonical mathematical facts and require a source or explicit local specification.

knowledge_statements.title: Unscaling Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error amplification when scaled iterates are mapped back to original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose scaled and original variables are related by \(x=E\widetilde x\) and \(y=D^*\widetilde y\), where \(D\) and \(E\) are invertible. Perturbations satisfy
\[
\Delta x=E\Delta\widetilde x,
\qquad
\Delta y=D^*\Delta\widetilde y,
\]
and hence
\[
\|\Delta x\|\leq\|E\|\,\|\Delta\widetilde x\|,
\qquad
\|\Delta y\|\leq\|D\|\,\|\Delta\widetilde y\|.
\]
Thus small scaled-coordinate errors may become large after unscaling when either operator norm is large; original-coordinate residuals and certificates must be recomputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mapping scaled iterates back to original coordinates can amplify their errors by the norms of the inverse coordinate transformations.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) and \(E\) are invertible linear scaling operators.
\(x=E\widetilde x\) and \(y=D^*\widetilde y\).
Errors are measured in compatible induced norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unscaled errors can be amplified by factors \(\|E\|\) and \(\|D\|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: induced-norm perturbation bounds for coordinate transformations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The induced-norm perturbation bounds are correct and property fits the leaf, but the solver-level requirement to recompute original-coordinate diagnostics is unsourced. The plain statement also calls the displayed unscaling maps inverse transformations without explicitly identifying them as inverses in the mathematical statement.

children.title: Overflow Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by magnitudes exceeding the representable numerical range.

knowledge_statements.title: Overflow Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-range overflow in residual, scaling, and cone-projection computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb F\) be a floating-point system whose largest finite magnitude is \(\Omega\). For an elementary operation with finite floating-point inputs and exact real result \(z\), an overflow failure occurs when \(|z|>\Omega\), so the computed result is an infinity, a saturated value, or an exception rather than a finite approximation to \(z\). Any solver residual, normalization, step length, or cone projection depending on that result is numerically invalid unless the operation is rescaled or evaluated in a wider range. Thus \(|z|=\Omega\) is the finite-range boundary for the operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overflow occurs when an exact intermediate exceeds the largest finite floating-point number, invalidating any solver diagnostic or update that depends on it.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb F\) has largest finite magnitude \(\Omega<\infty\).
The exact operation result \(z\) is well-defined over the reals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|z|>\Omega\) implies that no finite floating-point result can represent \(z\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable citation is supplied. The claim also conflates the largest finite representable magnitude with the rounding-mode-dependent overflow threshold: an exact result slightly larger than the largest finite value can round to that finite value in some modes. A numerical-arithmetic source is required to fix the boundary and possible outcomes.

children.title: Underflow Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by small magnitudes collapsing below useful numerical resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Underflow Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of tiny quantities through finite-range rounding or flushing to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta>0\) be the least positive representable magnitude, including subnormals when supported. If an exact nonzero intermediate \(z\) satisfies \(0<|z|<\eta/2\) under round-to-nearest, its computed value is zero. An underflow failure occurs when this zeroing, or implementation-defined flushing of values below a threshold, removes a component needed to evaluate a cone constraint, residual, scaling factor, or stopping test. The solver may then report a false zero residual, lose a search direction, or perform division by a computed zero. The boundary depends on the active underflow mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underflow failure occurs when a required tiny nonzero quantity rounds or flushes to zero, corrupting a residual, direction, scaling, or stopping decision.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic uses round-to-nearest or a specified flush-to-zero mode.
The discarded quantity affects a solver computation or diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(0<|z|<\eta/2\), round-to-nearest returns zero, so relative information about \(z\) is lost.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable citation supports the round-to-nearest, subnormal, tie, or flush-to-zero assertions. The mathematical version depends on the precise floating-point format and active underflow mode, so a targeted numerical-arithmetic source is required.

children.title: Loss-of-Significance Failures
children.top_down_role: Accuracy loss caused by cancellation or operations involving severely mismatched magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss-of-Significance Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cancellation-induced destruction of relative accuracy in conic-solver quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let floating-point subtraction satisfy \(\operatorname{fl}(a-b)=(a-b)+e\), with \(|e|\leq u(|a|+|b|)\) to first order in unit roundoff \(u\). When \(a\) and \(b\) have the same sign and \(|a-b|\ll |a|+|b|\), the relative error obeys \(|e|/|a-b|\leq u(|a|+|b|)/|a-b|\), which can be large. A loss-of-significance failure occurs when such cancellation makes the computed residual, gap, normalization, or cone-boundary distance insufficiently accurate for the decision tolerance used by the solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting nearly equal quantities can amplify rounding error enough to make a residual, gap, or cone-boundary decision unreliable.
assumptions_latex: Floating-point arithmetic has unit roundoff \(u\).
The subtraction result is finite and does not underflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative-error amplification factor is bounded to first order by \((|a|+|b|)/|a-b|\), and becomes unbounded as \(a-b\to0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable citation is supplied. A source must clarify whether the error model includes errors already present in the operands, since subtraction of exact floating-point operands has a stronger relative rounding model when the result is normal; cancellation primarily amplifies inherited operand errors.

children.title: Finite-Range Failure Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable solver symptoms used to distinguish finite-range numerical failures.

assumptions_latex: The arithmetic status, computed quantities, and relevant operands are logged.
The parameters satisfy \(u>0\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A triggered check flags a finite-range arithmetic hazard requiring recomputation, rescaling, or further error analysis; the cancellation check alone does not certify that the actual relative error exceeds \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: least positive representable magnitude used by the diagnostic

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime warning condition for overflow, underflow, and cancellation hazards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each monitored computed solver quantity \(q\), record its value, relevant operand magnitudes, and arithmetic status. A finite-range warning is triggered if at least one of the following holds: \(q\) is nonfinite; a quantity required to be nonzero by the monitored computation is returned as zero under the active underflow or flush-to-zero mode; or a subtraction \(q=\operatorname{fl}(a-b)\) has indicator \(\chi=(|a|+|b|)/\max(|q|,\eta)\) satisfying \(u\chi>\tau\). The last predicate says that the associated first-order a priori error bound exceeds the diagnostic budget; it is a warning condition, not a certificate that the realized error exceeds that budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The runtime diagnostic warns about nonfinite results, destructive zeroing of required quantities, and cancellation whose a priori error bound exceeds the configured budget; a warning does not by itself prove the realized error is too large.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Range Failure Diagnostics
Ill-Conditioned Cone-Splitting Stall
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stall condition for a fixed-point cone-splitting iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^{k+1}=T(z^k)\) and fixed-point residual \(r_k=\|T(z^k)-z^k\|\). Over a window of \(m\geq2\) iterations, an ill-conditioned cone-splitting stall is diagnosed when \(r_{k-m}>\varepsilon\), \(r_k/r_{k-m}\geq1-\delta\), and a local linearization \(I-J_T(z^k)\) has estimated condition number at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}\). The first two predicates establish inadequate progress above tolerance; the third attributes that stall to near-singularity of the local fixed-point equations rather than successful convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A splitting iteration is stalled when its residual remains above tolerance, barely decreases over a window, and the local fixed-point equations are ill-conditioned.
assumptions_latex: The fixed-point map \(T\) is locally differentiable at the monitored iterate.
\(0<\delta<1\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three displayed predicates constitute the ill-conditioned stall diagnostic.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is a plausible operational diagnostic, but no source supports the residual window, condition-number estimator, warning threshold, or causal attribution of the stall to ill-conditioning. Those solver-specific choices require an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Slow Tail Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed residual criterion for asymptotically slow solver progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k>0\) be a solver residual and let \(m\geq2\). Slow tail convergence at iteration \(k\) is diagnosed when \(r_k>\varepsilon\), the residual is nonincreasing on \(k-m,\ldots,k\), and \((r_k/r_{k-m})^{1/m}\geq q_{\mathrm{slow}}\) for a prescribed \(q_{\mathrm{slow}}\in(0,1)\) close to one. Equivalently, the observed geometric reduction per iteration is no better than \(q_{\mathrm{slow}}\). This condition distinguishes continuing but inadequate tail progress from a strict stall or an increasing residual sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slow tail convergence means the residual still decreases, but its windowed geometric reduction factor is too close to one above the target tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Residuals in the monitoring window are positive.
\(0<\varepsilon\) and \(0<q_{\mathrm{slow}}<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((r_k/r_{k-m})^{1/m}\geq q_{\mathrm{slow}}\) certifies inadequate observed tail contraction over the window.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The windowed contraction calculation is internally coherent and the condition kind fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular diagnostic or the interpretation of its configured threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Oscillatory Primal–Dual Progress
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed detection of alternating primal–dual updates without envelope contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w^k=(x^k,y^k)\) collect primal and dual iterates, \(d_k=w^k-w^{k-1}\), and \(r_k\) be a combined primal–dual residual. Oscillatory progress over a window is diagnosed when at least \(m-1\) consecutive direction pairs satisfy \(\langle d_j,d_{j-1}\rangle\leq-\gamma\|d_j\|\|d_{j-1}\|\), while \(\min_{k-m\leq j\leq k}r_j>(1-\delta)r_{k-m}\). Here \(\gamma\in(0,1]\) measures reversal and \(\delta\in(0,1)\) is required envelope reduction. The condition records repeated direction reversal without sufficient residual improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal–dual progress is oscillatory when successive updates repeatedly reverse direction while the best residual in the window fails to improve sufficiently.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual iterates share a specified product-space inner product.
\(m\geq2\), \(0<\gamma\leq1\), and \(0<\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reversal and residual-envelope predicates jointly diagnose oscillatory primal–dual progress.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the combined residual, product-space metric, or thresholds. In addition, the phrase 'at least m-1 consecutive direction pairs' does not explicitly specify the index range, so the exact operational predicate remains ambiguous pending a sourced formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Step-Size Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp relaxed fixed-point counterexample beyond the safe step interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the relaxed fixed-point iteration \(z^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda(Tz^k-z^k)\), nonexpansiveness of \(T\) alone does not ensure convergence when \(\lambda>1\). Indeed, on \(\mathbb R\), choose the nonexpansive map \(Tz=-z\), whose unique fixed point is zero. Then \(z^{k+1}=(1-2\lambda)z^k\). For every \(z^0\neq0\), the iterates diverge in magnitude whenever \(\lambda>1\), because \(|1-2\lambda|>1\); at \(\lambda=1\), they oscillate without convergence. Thus the boundary \(\lambda=1\) is sharp for a uniform guarantee over arbitrary nonexpansive maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For arbitrary nonexpansive splitting maps, relaxation at one can oscillate and any larger step can diverge; the map sending a scalar to its negative proves sharpness.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is only assumed nonexpansive.
The relaxation parameter \(\lambda\) is constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No convergence guarantee uniform over all nonexpansive \(T\) is possible for \(\lambda\geq1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar counterexample and sharp boundary are mathematically coherent, and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but no inspectable fixed-point source is supplied for the claimed uniform-guarantee boundary.

assumptions_latex: Restart events and positive monitored residuals are logged consistently.
The parameters satisfy \(L\geq1\), \(R\geq2\), and \(0<\delta<1\).
The indices \(p\) and \(q\) are integers satisfying \(0\leq p<q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The short-interval, restart-count, and insufficient-reduction predicates jointly diagnose restart thrashing over restart indices \(p,\ldots,q\).

notation.meaning: positive monitored residual at iteration k
minimum number of restart events in the window

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated restart detection without commensurate residual improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let restart times satisfy \(t_0<t_1<\cdots\), and let \(r_k>0\) be the monitored solver residual. Restart thrashing over restart indices \(p,\ldots,q\) is diagnosed when \(t_{i+1}-t_i\leq L\) for every \(i=p,\ldots,q-1\), the window contains at least \(R\) restart events so that \(q-p+1\geq R\), and \(r_{t_q}/r_{t_p}\geq1-\delta\). These predicates mean that the restart controller repeatedly discards algorithmic state within short intervals without achieving the prescribed net residual reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart thrashing is diagnosed when at least the prescribed number of restarts occur at short intervals and the residual fails to achieve the required net reduction across the restart window.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Thrashing

assumptions_latex: The perturbed outer iteration satisfies \(\|d_{k+1}\|\leq\rho\|d_k\|+\eta_k\).
The parameters satisfy \(0\leq\rho<1\), \(\eta_k\geq0\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(B_k>\varepsilon\), the stated perturbation bounds do not certify outer-iterate error at most \(\varepsilon\); if \(\eta_j\leq\bar\eta\), the corresponding asymptotic upper bound is \(\bar\eta/(1-\rho)\).

notation.meaning: outer-iterate deviation from the exact fixed point
linear-solve perturbation bound at iteration k
accumulated upper bound on outer-iterate error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic condition for accumulated inexact linear-solve error exceeding an outer accuracy budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an exact outer iteration is contractive with factor \(0\leq\rho<1\), while inexact linear solves yield perturbation bounds \(\eta_k\geq0\) and deviations satisfying \(\|d_{k+1}\|\leq\rho\|d_k\|+\eta_k\). Define \(B_k=\rho^k\|d_0\|+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\rho^{k-1-j}\eta_j\). Then \(\|d_k\|\leq B_k\). For a requested accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\), inaccurate linear-solve accumulation is flagged when \(B_k>\varepsilon\), because these perturbation bounds no longer certify the requested outer accuracy. If \(\eta_j\leq\bar\eta\), then \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}B_k\leq\bar\eta/(1-\rho)\); this is an upper bound and does not by itself prove a nonzero realized error floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometrically accumulated linear-solve error is flagged when its upper bound exceeds the requested outer accuracy. Uniformly bounded solve errors give an asymptotic upper bound, but do not prove that the realized error has a nonzero floor.
knowledge_statements.title: Inaccurate Linear-Solve Accumulation
Projection Root-Finding Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner scalar-root error that invalidates a cone-projection tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a cone projection is parameterized by the unique root \(\lambda_*\) of a continuous strictly monotone function \(\phi\), and the projected point is \(P(v)=p(\lambda_*)\). An inner root-finding failure occurs when the returned \(\widehat\lambda\) neither lies in a certified sign-changing bracket of width at most \(\varepsilon_\lambda\) nor satisfies a residual-to-root bound \(|\phi(\widehat\lambda)|/m\leq\varepsilon_\lambda\), where \(|\phi'(\lambda)|\geq m>0\) on the bracket. If \(p\) is \(L_p\)-Lipschitz, projection accuracy \(\|p(\widehat\lambda)-P(v)\|\leq\varepsilon_P\) requires \(L_p\varepsilon_\lambda\leq\varepsilon_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection root-finding fails when neither a narrow valid bracket nor a conditioned residual bound guarantees the requested cone-projection accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) has a unique root and satisfies \(|\phi'|\geq m>0\) on the certified bracket.
The map \(p\) is \(L_p\)-Lipschitz there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a root-error certificate satisfying \(L_p\varepsilon_\lambda\leq\varepsilon_P\), the requested projection tolerance is not certified.

notation.meaning: exact scalar root defining the projection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic root-error and Lipschitz implications are plausible, but no inspectable source establishes that the relevant cone projection has the stated unique monotone root parameterization, derivative bound, or projection map. A cone-specific source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Projection Rank Misclassification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue-gap boundary for reliable projected-rank determination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X^{\mathsf T}\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_i(X)\), and suppose spectral projection retains modes satisfying \(\lambda_i(X)>\tau\). If the computed matrix is \(\widehat X=X+E\), Weyl's bound gives \(|\lambda_i(\widehat X)-\lambda_i(X)|\leq\|E\|_2\). Therefore mode \(i\) is certainly retained when \(\lambda_i(\widehat X)>\tau+\|E\|_2\), certainly discarded when \(\lambda_i(\widehat X)<\tau-\|E\|_2\), and rank-ambiguous otherwise. Declaring a definite rank for an eigenvalue in this uncertainty band is a spectral-projection rank misclassification risk; no perturbation-based rank certificate follows from the stated error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected rank is reliable only for computed eigenvalues outside the threshold’s perturbation band; eigenvalues inside that band are classification-ambiguous.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(\widehat X\) are real symmetric.
A valid spectral-norm error bound \(\|E\|_2\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any computed eigenvalue satisfying \(|\lambda_i(\widehat X)-\tau|\leq\|E\|_2\) has uncertified threshold classification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbation-band criterion is mathematically coherent for consistently ordered eigenvalues of symmetric matrices, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. However, no inspectable matrix-perturbation citation is supplied for Weyl's bound or the resulting classification certificate.

assumptions_latex: The exact fixed-point map \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) has a fixed point \(z^*\) and satisfies \(\|T(u)-T(v)\|\le q\|u-v\|\) for some \(0\le q<1\).
The implemented iteration is \(z_{k+1}=T(z_k)+e_k\), where \(e_k\) is the aggregate inner-oracle error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(k\ge1\), \[\|z_k-z^*\|\le q^k\|z_0-z^*\|+\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-i}\|e_i\|.\] At iteration \(k\), approximate-oracle error is dominant when \[\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-i}\|e_i\|\ge q^k\|z_0-z^*\|.\] Under this diagnostic, reducing the outer fixed-point error alone cannot improve the displayed upper bound unless the weighted inner-error contribution is also reduced.

notation.meaning: Contraction factor of the exact operator.
Aggregate error in the approximate oracle at iteration \(k\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard perturbation bound for an inexact contractive fixed-point iteration
exact diagnostic threshold requires solver-interface source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contractive fixed-point version with additive inner-oracle errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the inexact iteration \(z_{k+1}=T(z_k)+e_k\). Contractivity and the triangle inequality give the diagnostic envelope \[\|z_k-z^*\|\le q^k\|z_0-z^*\|+\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-i}\|e_i\|.\] Define the oracle contribution \(E_k:=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-i}\|e_i\|\) and the exact-iteration contribution \(X_k:=q^k\|z_0-z^*\|\). Approximate-oracle error dominance occurs when \(E_k\ge X_k\). In that regime the computable convergence envelope is governed at least as strongly by accumulated inner errors as by exact outer contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a contractive outer iteration, oracle error dominates when its geometrically weighted accumulation is at least the remaining error predicted for exact iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Oracle Error Dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbation envelope is standard and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this solver-facing dominance threshold. The conclusion also overstates the consequence: reducing the outer contribution can still decrease the displayed bound while the inner-error term remains fixed, although it cannot reduce the inner-error floor.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), Anderson acceleration forms a residual-difference matrix \(F_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m_k}\).
The coefficient vector is computed from a least-squares problem using the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Anderson least-squares subproblem is numerically ill-conditioned at tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{AA}}>0\) when \[\sigma_{\min}(F_k)\le \tau_{\mathrm{AA}}\sigma_{\max}(F_k),\] with the convention that rank deficiency gives \(\kappa_2(F_k)=+\infty\). Equivalently, \(\kappa_2(F_k)\ge\tau_{\mathrm{AA}}^{-1}\). In this regime relative perturbations in residual history can be amplified by the least-squares coefficient computation by a factor comparable to \(\kappa_2(F_k)\).

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns are Anderson residual differences.
Spectral condition number, with value \(+\infty\) for rank deficiency.

review_flags: Anderson-specific threshold convention requires interface confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning diagnostic for the Anderson residual-history least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Anderson subproblem \[\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k}}\|f_k-F_k\gamma\|_2,\] define \(\kappa_2(F_k):=\sigma_{\max}(F_k)/\sigma_{\min}(F_k)\) when \(F_k\) has full column rank and \(\kappa_2(F_k):=+\infty\) otherwise. Given \(\tau_{\mathrm{AA}}>0\), the subproblem is diagnostically ill-conditioned precisely when \(\sigma_{\min}(F_k)\le\tau_{\mathrm{AA}}\sigma_{\max}(F_k)\), equivalently \(\kappa_2(F_k)\ge\tau_{\mathrm{AA}}^{-1}\). This condition identifies residual histories for which small data perturbations can produce large coefficient perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anderson mixing is ill-conditioned when its residual-difference matrix is rank deficient or its smallest singular value is too small relative to its largest.
knowledge_statements.title: Anderson Least-Squares Ill-Conditioning

assumptions_latex: An accelerated candidate has the affine form \(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}}=\sum_{j=0}^{m_k}\alpha_jT(z_{k-j})\) with \(\sum_j\alpha_j=1\).
Each evaluated image is perturbed by \(d_j\) satisfying \(\|d_j\|\le\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perturbed accelerated candidate satisfies \[\left\|\sum_{j=0}^{m_k}\alpha_j\bigl(T(z_{k-j})+d_j\bigr)-z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}}\right\|\le\delta_k\|\alpha\|_1.\] This bound is sharp over admissible perturbations. Thus extrapolation is unstable at an amplification threshold \(G_{\\max}\ge1\) when \(\|\alpha\|_1>G_{\\max}\), since oracle or rounding errors may then be amplified beyond the permitted factor.

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on perturbations of stored operator images.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: norm bound for affine combinations of perturbed vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation-amplification boundary for affine Anderson extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}}:=\sum_{j=0}^{m_k}\alpha_jT(z_{k-j})\), where \(\sum_j\alpha_j=1\). If stored or computed images are \(T(z_{k-j})+d_j\) with \(\|d_j\|\le\delta_k\), then \[\left\|\sum_{j=0}^{m_k}\alpha_jd_j\right\|\le\delta_k\sum_{j=0}^{m_k}|\alpha_j|=\delta_k\|\alpha\|_1.\] The bound is attained by aligned perturbations with signs matching the coefficients. For a prescribed admissible gain \(G_{\max}\), unstable extrapolation is therefore diagnosed by \(\|\alpha\|_1>G_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine extrapolation amplifies bounded evaluation errors by at most the coefficient one-norm; exceeding a configured gain marks unstable extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Extrapolation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind and the coefficient-one-norm amplification statement fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the configured gain as a solver diagnostic. The conclusion_latex field also contains the malformed token G_{\\max}; statement_latex itself uses valid delimited TeX.

assumptions_latex: At each iteration \(k\), a base candidate \(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and an accelerated candidate \(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}}\) are available.
A safeguard accepts acceleration only if \(\Phi(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}})\le\Phi(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{base}})-c\|z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}}-z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{base}}\|^2\), where \(c\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Let \(a_k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate safeguard acceptance. For a window length \(W\ge1\) and threshold \(\rho\in[0,1]\), iteration \(k\ge W-1\) lies in the safeguard-rejection regime when \[\frac1W\sum_{i=k-W+1}^{k}a_i\le\rho.\] The predicate is fully determined by the stated acceptance test, window, and threshold; \(\rho=0\) identifies windows in which every accelerated proposal is rejected.

notation.meaning: Safeguard merit function; smaller values are preferred.
Indicator that the accelerated candidate was accepted.
Window length and maximum accepted fraction defining the regime.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: empirical acceptance-rate predicate for a safeguarded acceleration method
acceptance test and threshold are interface conventions requiring source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed rejection-rate diagnostic under a merit-function safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(a_k=1\) when \[\Phi(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}})\le\Phi(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{base}})-c\|z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{acc}}-z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{base}}\|^2\] and define \(a_k=0\) otherwise. Given \(W\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(\rho\in[0,1]\), the safeguard-rejection regime holds at \(k\ge W-1\) exactly when \[W^{-1}\sum_{i=k-W+1}^{k}a_i\le\rho.\] Hence the diagnostic records sustained rejection rather than a single unsuccessful proposal; setting \(\rho=0\) requires rejection throughout the entire window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver is in the safeguard-rejection regime when the fraction of accepted accelerated proposals over a fixed window falls below a configured threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard-Rejection Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the terminal container, but the merit safeguard, window, and threshold are uncited interface conventions. The plain statement says the accepted fraction falls below the threshold, while the mathematical predicate uses a non-strict inequality.

assumptions_latex: The baseline method reaches the same stopping criterion in \(N_0\) iterations at per-iteration cost \(c_0>0\).
The accelerated method reaches it in \(N_A\) iterations and incurs nonnegative acceleration overhead \(h_k\) at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceleration overhead dominates its iteration savings precisely when \[N_Ac_0+\sum_{k=0}^{N_A-1}h_k\ge N_0c_0,\] equivalently \[\sum_{k=0}^{N_A-1}h_k\ge(N_0-N_A)c_0.\] This comparison concerns runs using the same stopping rule and cost units. If \(N_A\ge N_0\), dominance holds automatically because the overhead is nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Baseline and accelerated iteration counts to a common stopping criterion.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct total-cost comparison under a common stopping criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-work boundary comparing acceleration overhead with saved base iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Measure both runs in common cost units and against the same stopping criterion. The baseline work is \(C_0:=N_0c_0\), while accelerated work is \(C_A:=N_Ac_0+\sum_{k=0}^{N_A-1}h_k\). Acceleration-overhead dominance is the condition \[C_A\ge C_0,\] or equivalently \[\sum_{k=0}^{N_A-1}h_k\ge(N_0-N_A)c_0.\] Thus a reduction of \(N_0-N_A\) iterations is beneficial only when its base-work saving strictly exceeds the accumulated least-squares, safeguarding, and bookkeeping overhead represented by \(h_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration overhead dominates when its accumulated extra work is at least the base-iteration work saved before reaching the same stopping criterion.
knowledge_statements.title: Acceleration-Overhead Dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf and the cost comparison is algebraically correct under a common base cost per accelerated iteration. No inspectable source establishes that accounting model or the solver-interface meaning of the overhead terms.

children.title: Solver Diagnostic Interface Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting canonicalized cone programs, solver state, reported statuses, and downstream validation or escalation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: SCS Documentation
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: API data, cone metadata, settings, solution records, status values, and warm starts
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: SCS Documentation

assumptions_latex: The canonical slack belongs to a finite product cone \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_J\).
Each cone block has a fixed coordinate interval in the canonical slack vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid cone-block metadata determine a disjoint ordered partition \(0=o_1<o_2<\cdots<o_{J+1}=m\), dimensions \(d_j=o_{j+1}-o_j\), cone-family labels \(t_j\), and family parameters \(p_j\), such that \[s[o_j:o_{j+1}]\in K_j(t_j,p_j),\qquad K=\prod_{j=1}^J K_j(t_j,p_j).\] The metadata must additionally fix each block's vectorization convention and corresponding dual cone \(K_j^*\), making projection, residual, and dual-feasibility computations unambiguous.

notation.meaning: Canonical product cone and its component cones.
Starting offsets of the ordered cone blocks.
Cone-family label and family-specific parameters for block \(j\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a product-cone representation requires block dimensions, types, parameters, and coordinate conventions
exact metadata schema requires implementation source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural metadata for an ordered product-cone slack representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cone-block metadata for \(s\in\mathbb{R}^m\) are an ordered collection \(\mathcal{M}_K:=\{(o_j,o_{j+1},t_j,p_j,v_j)\}_{j=1}^J\) satisfying \(0=o_1<\cdots<o_{J+1}=m\). Here \(d_j:=o_{j+1}-o_j\), \(t_j\) identifies a cone family, \(p_j\) supplies its parameters, and \(v_j\) fixes its vectorization convention. They define \[K:=\prod_{j=1}^J K_j(t_j,p_j),\qquad s[o_j:o_{j+1}]\in K_j(t_j,p_j).\] Each entry must also determine the compatible dual block \(K_j^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-block metadata partition the slack coordinates and record each block's cone type, parameters, vectorization convention, and dual cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate kind for the metadata schema, and the product-cone partition is coherent. An implementation or interface source is required to establish that the listed fields, vectorization conventions, and dual-block information are the intended canonical metadata contract.

children.title: Variable Recovery Maps
children.top_down_role: Mappings from canonical solver variables to variables in the source formulation.

assumptions_latex: Canonicalization produces solver variables \(\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{\widehat n}\).
Original decision variables are assembled into \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) after undoing substitutions, eliminations, and scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A variable recovery map is an explicitly stored affine map \[R_x(\widehat{x})=P_x\widehat{x}+p_x\] whose output coordinates agree with the ordering and shapes of the original variables. For every canonical point generated from an original point \(x\), consistency requires \(R_x(C_x(x))=x\), where \(C_x\) is the canonicalization map on represented variables. Auxiliary canonical coordinates may lie in the null space of \(P_x\).

notation.meaning: Affine map recovering original variables from solver variables.
Canonicalization map from represented original variables to solver coordinates.
Stored linear recovery operator and offset.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine substitutions and eliminations compose into an affine recovery map
non-affine canonicalization variants and storage conventions require source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine recovery of original decision variables from canonical solver coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{\widehat n}\) denote the canonical solver variable and let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) concatenate the original decision variables in declared order. An affine variable recovery record is \((P_x,p_x)\), with \(P_x\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times\widehat n}\) and \(p_x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), representing \[R_x(\widehat{x}):=P_x\widehat{x}+p_x.\] If \(C_x\) embeds represented original variables into canonical coordinates, the required left-inverse condition is \(R_x(C_x(x))=x\) on the canonicalization domain. Shape metadata partition the output back into the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable recovery record is an affine map that reconstructs ordered, shaped original variables from canonical solver coordinates and reverses canonicalization on represented points.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Recovery Maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the recovery-map leaf, but the record restricts recovery to a stored affine map without evidence that the target interface excludes non-affine recovery procedures. The storage and shape conventions also lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Constraint Recovery Maps
children.top_down_role: Mappings from canonical rows or cone blocks to constraints in the source formulation.

assumptions_latex: The original model has constraint residual vector \(r(x)\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
The canonical solver record provides \((\widehat{x},\widehat{s})\) in its declared coordinate convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A constraint recovery map is a stored map \[R_c(\widehat{x},\widehat{s})=(r^{\mathrm{orig}},s^{\mathrm{orig}})\] returning original-order residuals and slacks with their declared shapes and signs. For every canonicalized original point \(x\), consistency requires \[R_c(C_x(x),C_s(x))=(r(x),s(x)),\] where \((C_x,C_s)\) is the primal canonicalization map. Any aggregation, duplicated constraint, or sign reversal must be encoded explicitly in \(R_c\).

notation.meaning: Map recovering original constraint residuals and slacks.
Canonicalization maps producing solver variables and slacks.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constraint transformations require an explicit inverse reporting map
generality beyond affine constraint transformations requires source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of original-order constraint residuals and slacks from canonical primal quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)\in\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(s(x)\) denote the original model's declared constraint residuals and slacks. A constraint recovery record specifies a map \[R_c:(\widehat{x},\widehat{s})\longmapsto(r^{\mathrm{orig}},s^{\mathrm{orig}}),\] including output ordering, shapes, signs, and any aggregation of canonical rows. If \((C_x(x),C_s(x))\) is the canonical representation of an original point, the recovery map must satisfy \[R_c(C_x(x),C_s(x))=(r(x),s(x)).\] Thus duplicated rows, introduced epigraph constraints, and sign changes cannot be inferred implicitly; their reporting disposition is part of the map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint recovery map converts canonical variables and slacks into original-order residuals and slacks while explicitly handling introduced, duplicated, or sign-reversed constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Recovery Maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the leaf and the round-trip requirement is internally meaningful, but no source fixes the meanings of original residuals and slacks or the treatment of introduced, duplicated, aggregated, and sign-reversed constraints.

children.title: Dual Quantity Recovery Maps
children.top_down_role: Mappings for reconstructing source-level dual quantities from canonical solver output.

assumptions_latex: The canonical primal transformation is \(\widehat{x}=D^{-1}x\), \(\widehat{s}=Es\), with invertible \(D\) and \(E\).
The scaled canonical objective is multiplied by \(\sigma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the conic pair \(Ax+s=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\), the compatible dual recovery map is \[R_y(\widehat y)=\sigma^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\widehat y.\] Indeed, if \(\widehat A=EAD\), \(\widehat c=\sigma D^{\mathsf T}c\), and \(\widehat y=\sigma E^{-\mathsf T}y\), then \(\widehat A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+\widehat c=\sigma D^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}y+c)\). Hence recovered dual quantities preserve stationarity after undoing scaling.

notation.meaning: Primal variable and constraint scaling operators.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dual scaling follows from preserving the stationarity pairing
cone-preservation and sign conventions require authoritative interface source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual recovery for an invertibly scaled standard conic primal–dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), with dual stationarity \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\). Under \(x=D\widehat{x}\), \(\widehat{s}=Es\), \(\widehat A=EAD\), and \(\widehat c=\sigma D^{\mathsf T}c\), define \(\widehat y:=\sigma E^{-\mathsf T}y\). The dual recovery map is therefore \[R_y(\widehat y):=\sigma^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\widehat y.\] It is compatible with stationarity because \[\widehat A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+\widehat c=\sigma D^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}y+c).\] Block signs and dual-cone conventions must accompany this map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual recovery applies the transpose inverse of constraint scaling and reverses objective scaling so that canonical stationarity maps back to original stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Quantity Recovery Maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the leaf and the displayed dual recovery formula preserves the stated stationarity transformation. The cone, sign, and scaling conventions are uncited, and the plain phrase 'transpose inverse of constraint scaling' is ambiguous relative to the displayed recovery action E^{\mathsf T}.

children.title: Recovery Map Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Structural checks on dimensions, ordering, signs, scaling metadata, and source-model correspondence.

assumptions_latex: Primal recovery maps \(R_x,R_c\) and dual recovery map \(R_y\) are supplied with their canonicalization maps.
All vectors, cone blocks, and objective scaling conventions are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovery system passes consistency checking when dimensions and block shapes match, \[R_x(C_x(x))=x,\qquad R_c(C_x(x),C_s(x))=(r(x),s(x)),\] on test points in the canonicalization domain, and recovered duals satisfy the declared stationarity transformation. For paired slack and dual coordinates it must also preserve the scaled pairing, \[\langle\widehat{s},\widehat y\rangle=\sigma\langle s,y\rangle.\] A failed equality, incompatible dimension, or undeclared output coordinate is a verifiable recovery-interface defect.

notation.meaning: Variable, constraint, and dual recovery maps.
Objective scaling factor used by the canonical model.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: commuting-map and pairing identities directly verify recovery compatibility
test-domain and numerical tolerance conventions require source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic and dimensional certificate for a canonical recovery-map system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A recovery-map consistency certificate consists of dimension checks together with the commuting identities \[R_x(C_x(x))=x,\qquad R_c(C_x(x),C_s(x))=(r(x),s(x))\] for admissible test points \(x\). The recovered dual vector must satisfy the declared transformation of canonical stationarity into original stationarity. Moreover, whenever canonical scaling uses objective factor \(\sigma\), paired slack and dual recovery must obey \[\langle\widehat{s},\widehat y\rangle=\sigma\langle s,y\rangle.\] Exact symbolic equality or residuals below a declared numerical tolerance certify consistency; any shape mismatch or violated identity rejects the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistency checks verify dimensions, round-trip primal recovery, transformed stationarity, and preservation of the scaled slack–dual pairing.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Map Consistency Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is a defensible kind for a record of passed recovery checks, and the pairing identity is consistent with the stated scaling family. No source specifies the test domain or tolerances, and checking identities only on unspecified test points does not by itself certify that functional identities hold throughout the canonicalization domain.

assumptions_latex: The original conic form is \(\min c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\) and \(s\in K\).
The scaling operators \(D\) and \(E\) are invertible, and \(E(K)=K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Canonicalization scale metadata are the tuple \((D,E,\sigma)\), with \(\sigma>0\), together with inverse-action rules, defining \[\widehat A=EAD,\quad \widehat b=Eb,\quad \widehat c=\sigma D^{\mathsf T}c,\quad x=D\widehat x,\quad \widehat s=Es.\] They imply \(\widehat A\widehat x+\widehat s=\widehat b\) exactly when \(Ax+s=b\), and \(\widehat c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x=\sigma c^{\mathsf T}x\). Zero scalings or inconsistent inverse rules make canonical recovery undefined.

notation.meaning: Invertible variable and constraint scaling operators.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invertible diagonal equilibration of standard conic form
specific solver scaling conventions require authoritative interface source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible scaling metadata for standard primal conic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\) and \(s\in K\), canonicalization scale metadata comprise invertible operators \(D\) and \(E\), a factor \(\sigma>0\), and their inverse-action conventions. They define \[x=D\widehat x,\quad\widehat s=Es,\quad\widehat A=EAD,\quad\widehat b=Eb,\quad\widehat c=\sigma D^{\mathsf T}c.\] The requirement \(E(K)=K\) preserves cone membership. Consequently, primal feasibility is equivalent in both coordinate systems and \(\widehat c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x=\sigma c^{\mathsf T}x\). The metadata must retain enough information to apply \(D^{-1}\), \(E^{-1}\), and \(\sigma^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale metadata record invertible variable, constraint, and objective scalings so feasibility, cone membership, objectives, and recovery remain unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonicalization Scale Metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the scale-metadata leaf, and the displayed transformations are algebraically consistent under the stated invertibility and cone-automorphism assumptions. An authoritative interface source is still required for the exact tuple, objective convention, and inverse-action requirements.

assumptions_latex: The solver addresses \(\min c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), with dual stationarity \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\), \(y\in K^*\).
Residual norms use declared data normalizations and a declared inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A primal–dual solution record is \[\mathcal S=(x,s,y,p,d,r_p,r_d,g,\mu),\] where \(p=c^{\mathsf T}x\), \(d=-b^{\mathsf T}y\), \(r_p=Ax+s-b\), \(r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+c\), \(g=p-d\), and \(\mu=\langle s,y\rangle\). The record is internally consistent only if these identities hold in the reported scaling and \(s\in K\), \(y\in K^*\); normalized residuals may be stored additionally but must declare their denominators.

notation.meaning: Reported primal variable, slack, and dual variable.
Primal residual, dual residual, duality gap, and complementarity pairing.

review_flags: sign and normalization conventions must be matched to the solver interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form conic primal–dual record with explicit residual and gap conventions.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal form \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), and dual convention \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\), \(y\in K^*\), a primal–dual solution record is \[\mathcal S:=(x,s,y,p,d,r_p,r_d,g,\mu),\] with \[p:=c^{\mathsf T}x,\quad d:=-b^{\mathsf T}y,\quad r_p:=Ax+s-b,\quad r_d:=A^{\mathsf T}y+c,\] and \[g:=p-d,\qquad\mu:=\langle s,y\rangle.\] The record must state whether quantities are scaled or recovered and must attach denominators to any normalized residuals. Internal consistency requires the displayed identities and the declared cone memberships.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual solution record stores primal, slack, and dual vectors together with objectives, feasibility residuals, duality gap, complementarity, scaling, and normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Solution Records

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

children.title: Infeasibility Certificate Records
children.top_down_role: Output fields carrying evidence for a reported infeasibility classification.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exact witness certifies infeasibility of the indicated side of the primal-dual pair; a tolerance-accepted approximate witness is a numerical diagnostic unless accompanied by rigorous error bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized diagnostic records for the standard primal-dual conic pair.

source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. An infeasibility-certificate record contains a type tag, a nonzero vector, its normalization, and verification residuals. A primal-infeasibility record stores \(y\in K^*\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). A dual-infeasibility record stores \((d_x,d_s)\neq(0,0)\) with \(Ad_x+d_s=0\), \(d_s\in K\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d_x<0\). A witness satisfying these conditions exactly is a mathematical certificate. A witness accepted only under numerical tolerances is an approximate diagnostic unless the record also supplies rigorous error bounds that imply the exact conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate record stores a normalized primal- or dual-infeasibility witness, its type, and verification residuals. An exact witness certifies infeasibility, while a tolerance-accepted approximate witness is only a numerical diagnostic unless rigorous error bounds validate it.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Certificate Records

source_witnesses.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

children.title: Primal Ray Records
children.top_down_role: Output fields representing reported primal recession or unboundedness directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Ray Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-checkable primal recession directions for a standard conic formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}\), a primal-ray record is a tuple containing \((d_x,d_s)\neq(0,0)\), a positive normalization scale, and residual measures such that \(Ad_x+d_s=0\), \(d_s\in K\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d_x<0\). If a primal feasible point exists, then \((x+t d_x,s+t d_s)\) is feasible for every \(t\geq0\), and its objective tends to \(-\infty\). The record therefore distinguishes the recession direction itself from any assertion that a feasible base point has been found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal ray is a normalized feasible recession direction with strictly negative objective slope; unboundedness additionally requires a feasible base point.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recorded direction proves dual infeasibility and, given primal feasibility, primal unboundedness below.

children.title: Dual Ray Records
children.top_down_role: Output fields representing reported dual recession or infeasibility directions.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dual ray satisfying the displayed conditions exactly certifies that the primal conic constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-checkable separating rays for primal infeasibility.

source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}\), a dual-ray record contains a nonzero vector \(y\), a positive normalization scale, and verification residuals satisfying \(y\in K^*\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). These conditions are homogeneous, so normalization does not alter validity. A vector satisfying them exactly certifies infeasibility of the primal conic constraints. Approximate records must report equality, cone-distance, and separating-margin residuals under an explicit tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-ray record stores a normalized dual-cone separator orthogonal to the constraint range and having a strictly negative pairing with the right-hand side; exact satisfaction of these conditions certifies primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Ray Records
