children.title: Certificate Provenance Metadata
children.top_down_role: Metadata describing scaling, normalization, accuracy, and solver context for reported evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Provenance Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reproducibility fields accompanying a solver-produced certificate or ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Certificate provenance metadata is represented by \(M=(v,p,i,k,\tau,n,h)\). Here \(v\) identifies the solver and version, \(p\) identifies the mathematical formulation and preprocessing map, \(i\) is the producing iteration, \(k\) names the certificate type, \(\tau\) records the verification tolerances, \(n\) records the normalization rule and scale, and \(h\) identifies the numerical backend and relevant settings. A certificate record is reproducible only if \(p\) includes enough information to map the stored vector back to the original problem and \(\tau\) determines every reported pass or failure decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provenance metadata identifies the solver, transformed problem, iteration, certificate type, tolerances, normalization, and backend needed to interpret and reproduce verification.
assumptions_latex: The associated certificate may have been produced for a scaled or transformed conic problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) determines the certificate's interpretation, verification convention, and map to the original formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the metadata leaf, but the proposed tuple, mandatory fields, and reproducibility criterion are uncited interface-design claims. An authoritative solver schema or diagnostic-interface specification with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Residual Records
children.top_down_role: Reported feasibility, optimality, gap, and certificate residual fields.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-level optimality and cone-feasibility diagnostics for a standard conic pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal variables \((x,s)\) and dual variable \(y\), a residual record stores \(r_p=Ax+s-b\), \(r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+c\), the gap \(g=c^{\mathsf T}x+b^{\mathsf T}y\), and cone violations \(\delta_p=\operatorname{dist}(s,K)\) and \(\delta_d=\operatorname{dist}(y,K^*)\). It records absolute values and normalized values obtained from an explicitly named scaling rule. The record is evaluated only against tolerances declared for primal feasibility, dual feasibility, gap, and cone membership; missing or nonfinite quantities are marked unavailable rather than treated as zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual record stores primal and dual equations, objective gap, cone violations, normalized values, and the tolerances used to judge them.
assumptions_latex: The primal objective is \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) and the dual objective is \(-b^{\mathsf T}y\).
Norm and scaling conventions are fixed by the solver interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The record supplies the numerical quantities used to assess approximate primal–dual optimality.

notation.meaning: Distances to the primal and dual cones.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual formulas are consistent with the declared primal-dual sign convention, and a definition is an appropriate role for this record leaf. However, the asserted stored fields, normalization behavior, tolerance semantics, and unavailable-value convention require a cited diagnostic-interface source.

children.title: Iteration Records
children.top_down_role: Iteration counts and phase-specific progress counters exposed by the solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered progress snapshots indexed by solver updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An iteration record is represented by \(I_j=(j,u_j,o_j,R_j,T_j,q_j)\), where \(j\in\mathbb N_0\) is a monotonically increasing update index, \(u_j\) identifies the algorithmic phase, \(o_j\) contains available primal and dual objective estimates, \(R_j\) references the residual record computed from the same iterate, \(T_j\) references cumulative timing data, and \(q_j\) contains step-specific quantities such as step length or linear-solve accuracy. Every field is either tagged with the same iterate identity or explicitly marked stale or unavailable; thus values from different updates cannot silently form one diagnostic snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iteration record binds an update index and phase to contemporaneous objectives, residuals, timing, and step diagnostics, marking stale or unavailable values explicitly.
assumptions_latex: Progress records are emitted in nondecreasing algorithmic order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_j\) is a coherent diagnostic snapshot associated with update \(j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is appropriate for an iteration-record leaf, but the tuple fields, monotonicity requirement, stale-value semantics, and coherence rule are an uncited proposed schema rather than source-supported knowledge.

children.title: Timing Records
children.top_down_role: Setup, solve, oracle, linear-system, and validation timing fields.

knowledge_statements.title: Timing Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone wall-clock and component-time measurements for solver progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A timing record at iteration \(j\) is represented by \(T_j=(t_j^{\mathrm{wall}},t_j^{\mathrm{cpu}},t_j^{\mathrm{setup}},t_j^{\mathrm{lin}},t_j^{\mathrm{cone}},t_j^{\mathrm{comm}})\). Each available component is a nonnegative duration measured from a declared origin; cumulative components are nondecreasing in \(j\). The record identifies its clock, units, accumulation convention, synchronization policy, and whether component times overlap. Consequently, component durations are not required to sum to wall time unless the record explicitly declares a disjoint partition. Unsupported measurements are marked unavailable and are not encoded as zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A timing record stores cumulative wall, CPU, setup, linear-algebra, cone, and communication times together with clock, units, overlap, and synchronization conventions.
assumptions_latex: All recorded durations use a declared common unit.
The iteration index refers to a completed diagnostic sampling event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_j\) permits meaningful temporal comparisons without assuming that overlapping components add to wall time.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the terminal container and the overlap warning is mathematically sensible. The exact component list, cumulative semantics, synchronization policy, and unavailable-value encoding nevertheless need an authoritative timing or solver-interface source.

children.title: Record Sampling Metadata
children.top_down_role: Metadata governing the frequency, granularity, and aggregation of diagnostic records.

knowledge_statements.title: Record Sampling Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata defining when progress records are observed and emitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sampling metadata is represented by \(S=(P,J_0,J_f,D,L)\). The predicate \(P(j,t,e)\) states whether iteration \(j\), elapsed time \(t\), and event tag \(e\) trigger a record; \(J_0\) and \(J_f\) indicate whether initialization and termination are always sampled; \(D\) states whether skipped observations are dropped or aggregated; and \(L\) gives any maximum retained-record count. For periodic iteration sampling with stride \(q\geq1\), \(P(j,t,e)\) includes \(j\equiv0\pmod q\). The metadata must distinguish absence caused by sampling from an unavailable diagnostic value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling metadata defines triggering iterations, times, and events; mandatory endpoint samples; handling of skipped observations; and any retention limit.
assumptions_latex: Iteration indices and event tags are defined by the producing solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) determines which progress observations can appear in the output sequence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits sampling metadata, but the tuple, endpoint flags, aggregation policy, retention field, and trigger predicate are uncited interface conventions. A source defining the relevant sampling schema and event vocabulary is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Status Taxonomy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutually exclusive terminal interpretations of solver evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A terminal solver status belongs to \(\{\mathrm{optimal},\mathrm{primal\ infeasible},\mathrm{dual\ infeasible},\mathrm{indeterminate},\mathrm{failure}\}\), optionally qualified as accurate or inaccurate according to declared tolerances. The optimal status requires primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and gap tests. Primal infeasible and dual infeasible require validated certificate records of the corresponding type. Indeterminate means termination without sufficient evidence for those three mathematical conclusions, including iteration or time limits. Failure denotes invalid input, numerical breakdown, or backend error preventing a trustworthy conclusion. A termination reason is recorded separately and must not itself be interpreted as a mathematical certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Statuses separate approximate optimality and certified infeasibility from inconclusive termination and operational failure; stopping reasons remain distinct from mathematical conclusions.
assumptions_latex: All status tests refer to explicit feasibility, gap, and certificate tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each termination receives one primary status whose evidentiary requirements are determined by the taxonomy.

notation.meaning: Approximate primal–dual solution accepted by tolerance tests.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct role for a status taxonomy, and the separation of termination reasons from mathematical conclusions is appropriate. The cited self-dual-embedding section may support certificate mathematics but does not establish this five-status software vocabulary, exclusivity rule, accurate/inaccurate qualifiers, or failure semantics; a solver-interface source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Direct Backend
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backend contract for repeated sparse linear solves in a first-order conic method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a sparse linear system \(H z=r_j\) generated by the solver update and a numerical tolerance. Initialize by selecting an ordering, performing symbolic analysis, and computing a sparse factorization of \(H\), or of a declared regularized matrix \(H+E\). At iteration \(j\), solve the triangular factors for \(z_j\), optionally apply iterative refinement, and compute the reported residual \(\rho_j=\lVert H z_j-r_j\rVert\). Reuse symbolic or numeric factors only while their validity conditions hold. Output \(z_j\), \(\rho_j\), factorization and refinement diagnostics, regularization metadata, and a success or failure flag.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse direct backend factors the solver's sparse system, performs triangular solves and optional refinement, and reports residual, regularization, reuse, and failure diagnostics.
assumptions_latex: The solver update exposes a finite-dimensional sparse linear system.
Any regularization is recorded as part of the backend state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The backend returns a candidate solution and sufficient diagnostics to assess the requested linear solve.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate role for the backend leaf, but the proposed initialization, factor-reuse conditions, refinement behavior, outputs, and diagnostic contract are solver-dependent and unsupported by a cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Iterative Backend
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backend contract using operator evaluations instead of an assembled system matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input linear operators implementing \(v\mapsto Hv\), an optional preconditioner \(M^{-1}\), right-hand side \(r_j\), initial guess \(z_j^{(0)}\), tolerance \(\eta_j\), and iteration limit \(L_j\). Initialize the chosen Krylov or stationary iteration without assembling \(H\). Generate iterates \(z_j^{(\ell)}\) using only operator, vector, inner-product, and preconditioner operations. Stop when the declared residual criterion is at most \(\eta_j\), or when \(L_j\), breakdown, or cancellation occurs. Output the final iterate, achieved residual, operator and preconditioner counts, inner iterations, stopping reason, and any detected loss of numerical validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free backend iteratively solves through operator and preconditioner calls, stopping by an explicit residual rule and reporting work counts and breakdowns.
assumptions_latex: The operator and preconditioner domains and codomains are compatible.
The residual norm and relative scaling convention are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The backend returns an approximate linear-system solution with an auditable stopping record.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the backend leaf, but Krylov and stationary methods cannot share one reliable stopping and breakdown contract without specifying the selected method, operator assumptions, and residual rule. These choices and output fields require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: GPU Operator Backend
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Device-resident operator execution with explicit synchronization and diagnostic semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input device-compatible operators, conic projections, vectors, precision policy, and stopping parameters. Initialize device storage and transfer or construct immutable problem data, recording the device and numerical formats. At each outer iteration, execute operator products, vector updates, reductions, and cone projections on the device; synchronize before any host-visible stopping decision or diagnostic snapshot. Compute residuals using the declared accumulation precision and mark asynchronously pending values unavailable. Stop under the solver's mathematical criteria or a device error. Output the final vectors, residual records, kernel and transfer timing, synchronization points, precision metadata, and device failure status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A GPU backend runs operator, reduction, and cone-projection kernels on device, synchronizing diagnostic decisions and reporting precision, timing, transfers, and failures.
assumptions_latex: All operator and cone-projection implementations support the selected device formats.
Host-visible diagnostics are read only after the declared synchronization event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The backend produces solver iterates and diagnostics whose device execution and numerical precision are explicitly recorded.

notation.meaning: Synchronized residual data at iteration j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for the GPU backend leaf, but the synchronization, precision, timing, transfer, and failure contract is uncited and implementation-dependent. In addition, the notation entries for \(j\) and \(r_j\) are not actually used in the statement. A precise backend source is needed before selecting a reliable replacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Operator Backend
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed realization of conic-solver linear operators with globally consistent adjoints and reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a conic problem with linear map \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), a partition \(A=[A_1\;\cdots\;A_p]\), and conformal vectors \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\). Worker \(i\) computes \(u_i=A_i x_i\); an all-reduction returns \(Ax=\sum_{i=1}^p u_i\). For an adjoint request with \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), worker \(i\) returns \(A_i^{\mathsf T}y\), and concatenation yields \(A^{\mathsf T}y\). Global inner products, norms, stopping residuals, and cone-block statistics are formed by deterministic collective reductions. The backend returns the same operator interface as a serial implementation, up to declared floating-point reduction error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition operator products among workers, combine forward products by reduction, concatenate adjoint products, and compute all global diagnostics through declared collective reductions.
assumptions_latex: \(A=[A_1\;\cdots\;A_p]\) is a conformal column partition.
Every collective operation terminates and includes each worker contribution exactly once.
Cone projections are assigned by complete cone blocks or use an equivalent distributed projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The backend realizes \(A\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\), and global diagnostic quantities through distributed local computations and collective communication.

notation.meaning: number of workers or operator partitions
operator block assigned to worker i

children.title: Scaling-Failure Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Evidence indicating that scaling quality may be responsible for unreliable progress or output.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Failure Diagnosis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational certificate that poor convergence is sensitive to admissible diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let run \(0\) use the original formulation and run \(s\) an invertibly scaled formulation, with both outputs recovered to original coordinates. Fix \(\gamma>1\) and a common iteration or time budget. Define \(E_j=\max\{r_{p,j},r_{d,j},g_j\}\), where the terms are normalized primal residual, normalized dual residual, and normalized gap. A scaling-failure diagnosis is issued when \(E_s\le E_0/\gamma\), run \(s\) attains the requested tolerance while run \(0\) does not, and the recovered objectives and feasibility classifications agree within their declared comparison tolerances. The certificate records both scaling maps, budgets, residual histories, and recovery errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling failure is diagnosed when an invertible rescaling materially improves normalized convergence under equal resources without changing the recovered problem classification.
assumptions_latex: Both runs solve algebraically equivalent formulations under invertible scaling maps.
Residuals and gaps are evaluated in original coordinates with identical normalization.
The runs use the same resource budget and requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recorded comparison certifies sensitivity of the observed failure to scaling under the chosen factor \(\gamma\).

notation.meaning: maximum normalized diagnostic error for run j
normalized primal residual, dual residual, and gap

children.title: Alternative Scaling Configurations
children.top_down_role: Candidate equilibration, normalization, or manual scaling regimes for a renewed solve.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Scaling Configurations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generation of invertible scaling trials for a rescale-resolve diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given conic data \((A,b,c,K)\), choose positive diagonal matrices \(D_x\) and \(D_y\) and a scalar \(\sigma>0\). Form scaled variables and data so that \(x=D_x\hat x\), equality rows are multiplied by \(D_y\), and the objective is multiplied by \(\sigma\); retain only transformations preserving the represented cone or map the cone explicitly. Construct a finite trial set containing the identity, norm equilibration, and bounded variants obtained by clipping every diagonal entry to \([\ell,u]\), where \(0<\ell\le u<\infty\). Store each forward and inverse map for recovery and residual evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Create identity, equilibrated, and bounded diagonal scalings, retaining invertible maps that preserve or explicitly transform the cone.
assumptions_latex: The conic data are \((A,b,c,K)\) in finite-dimensional spaces.
Scaling bounds satisfy \(0<\ell\le u<\infty\).
Each accepted variable scaling preserves \(K\) or supplies its transformed cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns finitely many algebraically equivalent, recoverable scaling configurations.

notation.meaning: positive diagonal variable and row scalings

children.title: Resolved-Run Execution
children.top_down_role: Execution scope for a solver run using revised scaling metadata or settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolved-Run Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled reruns of equivalent scaled formulations with comparable resources and diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input scaling configurations \(S_1,\ldots,S_q\), a solver, tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and resource budget \(B\). For each \(S_k\), transform the conic data, initialize by the same declared policy, and run the solver until its stopping test reaches \(\varepsilon\) or consumes \(B\). Recover primal and dual outputs to original coordinates using \(S_k^{-1}\). Recompute normalized primal residual, normalized dual residual, duality gap, cone-membership error, and any infeasibility certificate on the original unscaled data. Return the complete histories, termination reason, consumed resources, recovered outputs, and transformation metadata for every run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rerun each scaled formulation under a common policy, recover outputs, and recompute every diagnostic against the original problem data.
assumptions_latex: Each \(S_k\) is invertible and defines an equivalent conic formulation.
All runs use the same tolerance \(\varepsilon\), budget \(B\), and initialization policy.
Original problem data remain available for independent diagnostic recomputation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every resolved run yields a comparable diagnostic record expressed in original coordinates.

children.title: Resolved-Run Comparison
children.top_down_role: Comparison of statuses, residuals, certificates, timings, and recovered quantities across scaling regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolved-Run Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant comparison predicate for original and rescaled solver runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For runs \(i\) and \(j\) recovered to original coordinates, define \(E_k=\max\{r_{p,k},r_{d,k},g_k,e_{K,k}\}\), using identical normalizations, and let \(W_k\) denote consumed work. Given tolerances \(\tau_E,\tau_o,\tau_x\), the runs are diagnostically consistent when their feasibility statuses agree, \(|v_i-v_j|\le\tau_o(1+\max\{|v_i|,|v_j|\})\), and their recovered outputs or certificates differ by at most \(\tau_x\) under the declared comparison norm. Run \(j\) is diagnostically superior when it is consistent and either \(E_j\le\tau_E<E_i\) with \(W_j\le W_i\), or \(E_j<E_i\) at equal work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare recovered runs using common residual normalization, work, status, objective, and output consistency; declare improvement only when problem conclusions remain consistent.
assumptions_latex: All compared diagnostics are recomputed on the original data.
Work and termination statuses use common definitions.
Comparison tolerances are fixed before inspecting the runs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate distinguishes consistent numerical improvement from a scaling-induced change in the represented problem or reported conclusion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the comparison leaf, but no source supports the aggregate error, work-based superiority predicate, objective comparison, output norm, or selected thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Tighten-Oracle-Accuracy Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escalation route for determining whether inexact operator or projection evaluations dominate solver residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an inexact oracle return \(\widetilde O_{\eta}(z)\) with certified error at most \(\eta\). Choose \(0<\theta<1\), initial accuracy \(\eta_0\), solver tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and common budget \(B\). Run the solver using \(\eta_k=\theta^k\eta_0\), warm-starting only if that policy is used for every comparison. After each run, independently recompute conic residuals with an oracle accuracy no larger than \(\min\{\eta_k,\varepsilon/10\}\). Stop when the reported classification and recomputed residuals stabilize within declared tolerances, or when the tightest available oracle accuracy is reached. Return the accuracy schedule and all recomputed diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly tighten certified oracle error and recompute diagnostics independently until the conclusion stabilizes or oracle accuracy cannot improve.
assumptions_latex: The oracle supplies a valid error bound \(\eta\) for each evaluation.
The sequence \(\eta_k=\theta^k\eta_0\) is available for \(0<\theta<1\).
Runs use a common solver tolerance and resource-accounting policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route tests whether the solver diagnosis is stable under decreasing oracle error.

notation.meaning: oracle evaluated with certified error bound eta

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic reduction of a conic system to an exposed face containing its feasible slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the feasibility system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), initialize \(F_0=K\). At stage \(k\), seek an exposing vector \(y_k\in F_k^*\) such that \(\langle y_k,x\rangle=0\) for every feasible \(x\), with \(y_k\notin F_k^{\perp}\). If found, set \(F_{k+1}=F_k\cap y_k^{\perp}\) and reformulate the system over \(F_{k+1}\). Stop when no such vector is found or the reduced system has a point in \(\operatorname{ri}F_k\). Record every exposing vector and validate its dual-cone membership and annihilation equations before resolving the reduced problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly expose proper faces containing all feasible points, validate each exposing vector, and resolve on the final reduced cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
Each exposing vector is validated against the current face and the affine constraints.
The facial-reduction oracle either returns a valid exposing vector or reports none.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update preserves the feasible set and replaces the current cone by a proper exposed face containing it.

dual cone of the current face in its ambient span

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Precision Validation Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent validation of solver outputs using arithmetic precision exceeding that of the original run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input original conic data, a candidate primal-dual output or infeasibility certificate, target tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and precisions \(p_0<p_1<\cdots<p_q\). At precision \(p_k\), reevaluate all affine residuals, objective values, cone-membership tests, complementarity quantities, and certificate identities directly from the original data, using directed error bounds when available. Accept the diagnosis only if the resulting upper bounds are at most \(\varepsilon\) and the classification is unchanged at two successive precisions. Otherwise increase precision; if no precision remains, return an unresolved validation result together with the final bounds and precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute every diagnostic from original data at increasing precision, accepting only stable classifications backed by residual upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: The original data and candidate output can be represented at every selected precision.
Cone-membership and linear-algebra evaluations provide reliable error bounds.
The validation tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is fixed before escalation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route returns a precision-stable validated diagnosis or an explicit unresolved result with numerical error bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the validation-route leaf, but no source supports the directed-error validation procedure, the requirement of stability at two successive precisions, or the stated acceptance guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Accuracy Solver Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escalation to a solver with stricter attainable tolerances or stronger local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a conic problem, baseline output, target tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and a secondary solver whose declared attainable accuracy is below \(\varepsilon\). Initialize the secondary solver from the baseline output only when its algorithm permits; otherwise use its standard initialization. Solve the identical unscaled problem, then independently recompute normalized primal feasibility, dual feasibility, duality gap, cone-membership error, and any certificate equations from the original data. Accept the escalated result when every required diagnostic is at most \(\varepsilon\) and its status is consistent with the recomputed quantities; otherwise report disagreement, resource exhaustion, or failure to reach accuracy without replacing the baseline record.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve the same problem with a more accurate solver and accept its conclusion only after independent original-data diagnostic checks.
assumptions_latex: The secondary solver supports the same cone and problem formulation.
Its declared attainable accuracy is stricter than \(\varepsilon\).
Both solver records retain outputs sufficient for independent residual evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route produces an independently checked higher-accuracy result or a documented unresolved discrepancy.

notation.meaning: recomputed normalized primal and dual residuals
